-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB67 - dti_calculation_log
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB67 - dti_calculation_log
-- Description: Snapshot table storing front-end and back-end DTI calculations
-- Business Case: The `dti_calculation_log` table is a snapshot table storing the precise calculations for a borrower's Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio at the moment of application submission and at any subsequent data change. It captures the gross monthly income, total housing payment (PITI), total other monthly debts, and the resulting front-end (housing) and back-end (total) ratios. This table is crucial for the real-time DTI feedback loop in the POS, allowing borrowers to see the exact impact of paying off a credit card or adjusting their loan amount. By storing the calculation inputs and outputs immutably, it provides underwriters and auditors with a transparent, mathematical proof of how the ratio was derived at any point in the loan lifecycle. It supports the AUS strategy engine by feeding it the exact DTI inputs used to determine loan eligibility.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `dti_calculation_log` table is eliminating the single largest cause of loan denials and rework: DTI miscalculation and borrower misalignment. Underwriters often discover late in the process that a borrower's DTI exceeds GSE limits due to an omitted debt or miscalculated income, resulting in a denied loan after weeks of work. By providing real-time, system-calculated DTI feedback at the POS, Hyperion empowers borrowers to self-correct before they even apply, drastically reducing the 60% abandonment rate for ineligible profiles. From a compliance standpoint, immutable logs of DTI calculations protect the lender from fair lending accusations, proving that denials were based on objective, mathematically sound criteria. Strategically, analyzing this data helps product managers identify if specific loan programs have DTI thresholds that consistently block good borrowers, informing capital markets to seek investors with more flexible overlays. This ensures operational efficiency and protects profit margins.
-- KPIs: DTI calculation accuracy, Real-time feedback latency, Loan denial rate due to DTI, Borrower self-correction rate, Underwriter DTI override frequency
-- Feature Reference: F-60, F-129
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.dti_calculation_log (
    -- Primary key
    dti_calculation_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Income inputs
    gross_monthly_income NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (gross_monthly_income >= 0),
    net_monthly_income NUMERIC(18,2),
    total_income_sources INTEGER DEFAULT 0,

    -- Housing expenses (PITI)
    principal_and_interest NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (principal_and_interest >= 0),
    property_taxes NUMERIC(12,2),
    homeowners_insurance NUMERIC(12,2),
    mortgage_insurance NUMERIC(12,2),
    hoa_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
    total_housing_expense NUMERIC(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        principal_and_interest + COALESCE(property_taxes, 0) +
        COALESCE(homeowners_insurance, 0) + COALESCE(mortgage_insurance, 0) +
        COALESCE(hoa_fees, 0)
    ) STORED,

    -- Total debt
    total_monthly_debt NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (total_monthly_debt >= 0),

    -- Ratios
    front_end_ratio NUMERIC(5,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        CASE
            WHEN gross_monthly_income = 0 THEN 0
            ELSE (total_housing_expense / gross_monthly_income) * 100
        END
    ) STORED,
    back_end_ratio NUMERIC(5,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        CASE
            WHEN gross_monthly_income = 0 THEN 0
            ELSE ((total_housing_expense + total_monthly_debt) / gross_monthly_income) * 100
        END
    ) STORED,

    -- Qualification
    is_qualified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    qualification_notes TEXT,

    -- Calculation context
    calculation_source VARCHAR(50) CHECK (calculation_source IN ('AUTO_REALTIME', 'AUS_SUBMISSION', 'UNDERWRITER', 'BORROWER_SELF')),
    calculation_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_dti_calculation_log_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT dti_calculation_log_ratio_check CHECK (
        front_end_ratio >= 0 AND front_end_ratio <= 100 AND
        back_end_ratio >= 0 AND back_end_ratio <= 100
    )
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.dti_calculation_log IS 'Snapshot table storing front-end and back-end DTI calculations, enabling real-time feedback and auditability';

-- Indexes for dti_calculation_log table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_application ON pos.dti_calculation_log (application_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_back_end_ratio ON pos.dti_calculation_log (back_end_ratio);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_front_end_ratio ON pos.dti_calculation_log (front_end_ratio);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_is_qualified ON pos.dti_calculation_log (is_qualified);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_calculation_timestamp ON pos.dti_calculation_log (calculation_timestamp);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dti_calculation_log_calculation_source ON pos.dti_calculation_log (calculation_source);

-- TABLE: DB68 - escrow_piti_component
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB68 - escrow_piti_component
-- Description: Breaks down Principal, Interest, Taxes, Insurance for escrow estimates
-- Business Case: The `escrow_piti_component` table breaks down the total monthly housing payment into its four constituent parts: Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance (PITI). It stores the calculated amount for each component, including private mortgage insurance (MI) and homeowner association (HOA) dues, linked to the specific application. This granular breakdown is essential for the POS "Escrow Estimate Visualizer," providing borrowers with complete transparency into what makes up their monthly obligation. It also acts as the input layer for the DTI calculation engine. By isolating the tax and insurance components, the system can dynamically adjust the escrow estimates when the property location changes or when the borrower toggles different MI coverage options. It ensures that the Loan Estimate generated at the POS is perfectly aligned with the final closing figures, preventing escrow shortfall shocks.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `escrow_piti_component` table is rooted in building borrower trust through transparency and preventing the operational fallout of payment shock. The number one complaint from new homeowners is that their actual monthly payment was higher than they expected, usually due to misunderstood escrow requirements for taxes and insurance. By decomposing and visually presenting the PITI components in real-time within the POS, Hyperion sets accurate expectations, reducing early payment defaults and increasing borrower satisfaction. Operationally, this structured data ensures that the initial Loan Estimate is flawless, avoiding TRID tolerance violations caused by under-estimated escrows. Strategically, this data allows the AI Core to identify opportunities for the borrower, such as flagging that a 20% down payment would eliminate the MI component entirely, nudging the borrower toward a more profitable loan product for the lender. This level of advisory intelligence transforms the POS into a trusted financial guide.
-- KPIs: PITI calculation accuracy, Escrow estimate vs. actual variance, MI option toggle rate, Borrower trust index, TRID escrow violation rate
-- Feature Reference: F-67, F-60
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.escrow_piti_component (
    -- Primary key
    escrow_piti_component_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- PITI components
    principal_amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (principal_amount >= 0),
    interest_amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (interest_amount >= 0),
    property_taxes_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0 CHECK (property_taxes_amount >= 0),
    homeowners_insurance_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0 CHECK (homeowners_insurance_amount >= 0),
    mortgage_insurance_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0 CHECK (mortgage_insurance_amount >= 0),
    hoa_fees_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0 CHECK (hoa_fees_amount >= 0),

    -- Total PITI
    total_monthly_payment NUMERIC(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        principal_amount + interest_amount + COALESCE(property_taxes_amount, 0) +
        COALESCE(homeowners_insurance_amount, 0) + COALESCE(mortgage_insurance_amount, 0) +
        COALESCE(hoa_fees_amount, 0)
    ) STORED,

    -- Calculation context
    interest_rate NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL,
    loan_term_months INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (loan_term_months IN (120, 180, 240, 300, 360, 480)),
    loan_amount NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (loan_amount >= 0),

    -- Escrow details
    escrow_establishment_amount NUMERIC(12,2),
    escrow_cushion_amount NUMERIC(12,2),
    escrow_payment_frequency VARCHAR(20) CHECK (escrow_payment_frequency IN ('MONTHLY', 'QUARTERLY', 'SEMI_ANNUAL', 'ANNUAL')),

    -- Status
    is_current BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_escrow_piti_component_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT escrow_piti_component_interest_rate_check CHECK (interest_rate >= 0 AND interest_rate <= 100)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.escrow_piti_component IS 'Breaks down Principal, Interest, Taxes, Insurance for escrow estimates, enabling transparent payment visualization';

-- Indexes for escrow_piti_component table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_escrow_piti_component_application ON pos.escrow_piti_component (application_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_escrow_piti_component_is_current ON pos.escrow_piti_component (is_current);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_escrow_piti_component_total_payment ON pos.escrow_piti_component (total_monthly_payment);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_escrow_piti_component_created_at ON pos.escrow_piti_component (created_at);

-- Table: DB71 - employment_gap_explanation
-- Description: Stores borrower explanations for gaps in employment > 30 days
-- Business Case: The `employment_gap_explanation` table captures the specific, written explanations provided by borrowers for gaps in employment exceeding 30 days, a strict requirement for GSE underwriting. It links directly to the `employment` table, storing the start and end dates of the gap and the borrower's narrative explanation (e.g., "Medical leave," "Returned to school"). This table transforms a common underwriting condition from a reactive, 11th-hour scramble into a proactive, structured data capture at the point of sale. By isolating these explanations, the AI Core can perform preliminary NLP analysis to flag potentially problematic reasons (e.g., "fired" vs. "laid off") and alert the Loan Officer to collect supporting documentation (like a termination letter) immediately. It provides a permanent audit trail of the borrower's attestation regarding their employment history.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `employment_gap_explanation` table is eliminating the delays and compliance risks associated with unexplained employment gaps. In traditional workflows, the system asks for employment dates, but rarely forces the user to explain gaps upfront. The underwriter discovers the gap weeks later, issues a condition, the processor emails the borrower, and days pass waiting for a written explanation. By capturing this data structurally during the POS flow, Hyperion short-circuits this cycle, saving days of latency. Furthermore, the NLP analysis of these explanations allows the AI to auto-generate the exact list of supporting documents needed to satisfy the underwriter, preventing rework. Strategically, aggregating this data allows product teams to refine the progressive disclosure logic; if a specific gap reason consistently leads to loan denial, the system can instantly advise the borrower of their ineligibility, saving the lender operational costs on dead files and preserving the borrower's trust.

    -- Gap details
    gap_start_date DATE NOT NULL,
    gap_end_date DATE NOT NULL,
    gap_duration_days INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gap_end_date - gap_start_date) STORED,

    -- Explanation
    explanation_text TEXT NOT NULL,
    explanation_category VARCHAR(50) CHECK (explanation_category IN ('MEDICAL', 'EDUCATION', 'JOB_SEARCH', 'CAREGIVING', 'RETIREMENT', 'SABBATICAL', 'OTHER')),

    nlp_processed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Verification
    verification_status pos.typ_verification_status_enum DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    verification_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

        REFERENCES pos.employment(employment_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_employment_gap_document FOREIGN KEY (supporting_document_upload_id)
        REFERENCES pos.document_upload(document_upload_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    CONSTRAINT employment_gap_dates_check CHECK (gap_end_date >= gap_start_date)
);

-- TABLE: DB73 - arm_disclosure_ack

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB73 - arm_disclosure_ack
-- Description: Tracks acknowledgment of Adjustable Rate Mortgage specific disclosures
-- Business Case: The `arm_disclosure_ack` table tracks the specific acknowledgment of Adjustable Rate Mortgage (ARM) program disclosures, capturing data distinct from general eConsent. It records the specific ARM parameters presented to the borrower at the time of disclosure, including the index, margin, adjustment caps, and initial fixed period. This table is legally mandated under Regulation Z, which requires lenders to provide specific, timely disclosures for ARM programs. By capturing the exact terms the borrower acknowledged, it prevents claims of "bait and switch" if rates adjust in the future. It links directly to the `disclosure_package` table, ensuring that this specific acknowledgment is bundled correctly. The table supports version control, ensuring that if the lender changes ARM products, the correct version of the disclosure is tied to the borrower's specific lock.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `arm_disclosure_ack` table is ensuring strict compliance with Reg Z and mitigating the legal risk of future borrower disputes regarding rate adjustments. ARM loans are inherently complex and can lead to payment shock, making them a prime target for CFPB audits and borrower litigation. If a lender cannot prove that the borrower understood the specific margin and caps of their ARM, they can be held liable for the increased interest payments. By structuring the capture of this acknowledgment within the POS, Hyperion ensures that no ARM application proceeds without a digitally signed, timestamped record of the exact program terms. Strategically, the data captured here allows executives to monitor which ARM products are most popular and how often borrowers lock into the initial rate vs. floating, providing critical data for capital markets hedging strategies. This table provides the legal armor necessary to offer complex products safely.
-- KPIs: ARM disclosure completion rate, Time from disclosure to acknowledgment, Audit pass rate for ARM compliance, Borrower dispute rate on ARM adjustments, ARM product popularity index
-- Feature Reference: F-110
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.arm_disclosure_ack (
    -- Primary key
    arm_disclosure_ack_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    disclosure_package_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- ARM parameters
    arm_index pos.typ_arm_index_enum NOT NULL,
    arm_margin NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL,
    arm_initial_fixed_years INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (arm_initial_fixed_years >= 1),
    arm_periodic_cap NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL CHECK (arm_periodic_cap >= 0),
    arm_lifetime_cap NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL CHECK (arm_lifetime_cap >= 0),
    arm_initial_rate NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL,
    arm_floor_rate NUMERIC(7,4),

    -- Additional details
    arm_interest_only_period_years INTEGER DEFAULT 0 CHECK (arm_interest_only_period_years >= 0),
    arm_negative_amortization_allowed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,

    -- Acknowledgment
    acknowledged_by UUID NOT NULL,
    acknowledged_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    acknowledgment_ip INET NOT NULL,

    -- Status
    is_current BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_arm_disclosure_ack_package FOREIGN KEY (disclosure_package_id)
        REFERENCES pos.disclosure_package(disclosure_package_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT arm_disclosure_ack_rates_check CHECK (
        arm_initial_rate >= 0 AND arm_initial_rate <= 100 AND
        arm_margin >= 0 AND arm_margin <= 100 AND
        arm_periodic_cap >= 0 AND arm_periodic_cap <= 100 AND
        arm_lifetime_cap >= 0 AND arm_lifetime_cap <= 100
    )
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.arm_disclosure_ack IS 'Tracks acknowledgment of Adjustable Rate Mortgage specific disclosures, enabling Reg Z compliance';

-- Table: DB74 - ppp_disclosure_ack

It captures the penalty term (e.g., 3 years), the maximum penalty percentage, and the borrower's eSignature. Due to the severe consumer protection regulations surrounding prepayment penalties—especially under TRID and state laws—this acknowledgment must be separate and highly visible from general eConsent. This table acts as a compliance firewall; the system will not allow a loan to proceed to closing with a PPP if this specific acknowledgment table is empty. It supports the AI validation engine, which cross-references the PPP term against state-specific limits (e.g., PPPs are illegal in certain states or on certain loan amounts) and automatically flags violations before the disclosure is even generated.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `ppp_disclosure_ack` table is preventing catastrophic regulatory fines and class-action lawsuits stemming from improperly disclosed prepayment penalties. The CFPB considers prepayment penalties a "trigger term" that requires exact, clear disclosure; failing to do so can result in the penalty being voided, the lender being fined, and the loan being subject to rescission. In legacy systems, the PPP is often buried in a checkbox, leading to compliance exposure. By isolating this acknowledgment into a dedicated, immutable table, Hyperion guarantees that the borrower explicitly agreed to the penalty terms. Operationally, the AI validation against state laws prevents the costly mistake of locking a loan with an illegal PPP, which would require re-disclosure and potential loss of lock. Strategically, this structured data protects the lender's secondary market execution, as investors will not buy loans with improperly documented prepayment penalties, ensuring zero repurchase risk.

    -- Penalty calculation
    penalty_calculation_method VARCHAR(50) CHECK (penalty_calculation_method IN ('PERCENTAGE_OF_LOAN', 'INTEREST_DIFFERENTIAL', 'FIXED_AMOUNT')),

-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB76 - magic_link_log
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB76 - magic_link_log
-- Description: Tracks generation and redemption of passwordless login links
-- Business Case: The `magic_link_log` table manages the lifecycle of secure, time-bound tokens used for passwordless authentication in the POS. When a borrower requests access via email or SMS, the system generates a unique, cryptographically hashed token and stores it here alongside an expiration timestamp and usage status. This table is the engine behind the frictionless "Save-and-Resume" and mobile-first login strategies. Instead of forcing users to remember complex passwords—a primary cause of session abandonment—the system validates the incoming token against this table. If the token is valid and unused, the user is authenticated instantly. The table tracks the IP address and device from which the link was generated and consumed, feeding the Zero-Trust security engine to detect anomalous access patterns, such as a link generated in the US but clicked from an overseas IP address. Once a token is consumed or expires, it is logically isolated to prevent replay attacks.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `magic_link_log` table is centered on eliminating password friction, thereby directly increasing application conversion rates and securing the authentication process. Industry data shows that up to 30% of returning users abandon the process at the login screen because they cannot remember their password or do not want to deal with a reset flow. By implementing a secure, token-based magic link system, Hyperion removes this barrier entirely, providing a one-click entry point that drastically reduces the 60% application abandonment rate. Operationally, it eliminates the immense IT helpdesk burden associated with password resets, lowering the cost per loan. Strategically, from a security perspective, magic links mitigate the risk of brute-force attacks and credential stuffing, as the tokens are single-use and short-lived. This ensures that the borrower experience remains zero-friction while maintaining the strict SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security posture required for handling sensitive financial PII.
-- KPIs: Magic link authentication success rate, Password reset request reduction, Token expiration rate, Replay attack intercept rate, Returning user session initiation time
-- Feature Reference: F-43
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.magic_link_log (
    -- Primary key
    magic_link_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    borrower_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Token details
    token_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    token_salt VARCHAR(64),

    -- Expiry
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    expiry_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,

    -- Usage
    is_used BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    used_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    used_ip INET,
    used_user_agent TEXT,

    -- Request context
    request_ip INET NOT NULL,
    request_user_agent TEXT,
    request_channel pos.typ_alert_channel_enum NOT NULL,

    -- Status
    is_revoked BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    revocation_reason TEXT,

    -- Audit trail
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_magic_link_log_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
        REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT magic_link_log_expiry_check CHECK (expiry_date >= created_at)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.magic_link_log IS 'Tracks generation and redemption of passwordless login links, enabling secure and frictionless authentication';

-- Table: DB77 - biometric_device_log
-- Description: Registers FaceID/TouchID usage for mobile app authentication
-- Business Case: The `biometric_device_log` table registers and tracks the usage of native mobile biometric authenticators (such as Apple FaceID and Android TouchID) for borrower access. It stores the mapped device ID, the type of biometric used, the registration date, and an encrypted public key reference (storing only the validation token, never the biometric template itself). This table acts as the secure bridge between the device's hardware-level security enclave and the Hyperion POS session manager. It enables the progressive profiling of the borrower's trusted devices; once a device is biometrically validated, the system can reduce the frequency of intrusive multi-factor authentication (MFA) challenges for that specific session. The table also logs failed biometric attempts, triggering fallback to password or magic link authentication, ensuring that security is never compromised for convenience.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `biometric_device_log` table is delivering a consumer-grade, frictionless mobile experience while adhering to the highest standards of Zero-Trust security. Mobile borrowers expect the same one-tap access they get from their banking apps; forcing them to type a complex password on a small screen destroys the user experience and drives abandonment. By supporting and tracking biometric authentication, Hyperion reduces the time-to-resume for a loan application to under a second, directly supporting the 3x faster application-to-close target. From a security standpoint, hardware-backed biometrics are exponentially more secure than passwords, mitigating the risk of account takeovers and PII exposure. Strategically, the data captured here allows product managers to measure the adoption rate of biometrics versus traditional login methods, enabling targeted UX improvements that nudge users toward the most secure and efficient authentication path, ultimately lowering operational risk and support costs.
-- KPIs: Biometric login adoption rate, Authentication latency reduction, Account takeover rate via compromised credentials, Fallback authentication rate, Mobile session abandonment rate
-- Feature Reference: F-62
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.biometric_device_log (
    -- Primary key

    -- Foreign keys
    mobile_device_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Biometric details
    biometric_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (biometric_type IN ('FACE_ID', 'TOUCH_ID', 'FINGERPRINT', 'IRIS', 'VOICE')),
    biometric_registration_id VARCHAR(100),
    public_key_encrypted TEXT,

    -- Registration
    registered_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    registration_ip INET,

    -- Usage
    last_used_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    usage_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    last_successful_use TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Failures
    failed_attempt_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    last_failed_attempt TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Status
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    is_revoked BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    revocation_reason TEXT,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

        REFERENCES pos.mobile_device(mobile_device_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB78 - ofac_scan_log
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB78 - ofac_scan_log
-- Description: Logs OFAC/sanctions list checks against borrower data at POS entry
-- Business Case: The `ofac_scan_log` table records the results of real-time sanctions and fraud list checks executed during the borrower onboarding process within the POS. Before a loan application proceeds deeply into the pipeline, the system checks the borrower's PII against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, as well as other governmental and international watch lists. This table captures the borrower ID, the specific list version checked, the timestamp, and the scan result (clear, potential match, or confirmed match). If a potential match is flagged, the table records the specific entities or aliases that triggered the alert, providing compliance officers with the necessary context to investigate. By embedding this scan directly at the point of sale, the table acts as the first line of defense against unauthorized and illegal transactions, ensuring that the system automatically blocks or quarantines high-risk applications immediately, before any Loan Officer time or vendor resources are wasted on an unprocessable file.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `ofac_scan_log` table is rooted in absolute regulatory compliance and institutional risk mitigation. Processing a transaction with a sanctioned individual or entity carries catastrophic legal and financial consequences, including massive federal fines and criminal liability. In traditional workflows, OFAC checks are sometimes performed manually or delayed until the underwriting stage, exposing the lender to risk and wasted operational effort. By automating and logging the OFAC scan at the very inception of the application, Hyperion guarantees that no prohibited party enters the loan pipeline. This table provides the immutable audit trail required by regulators to prove that the lender maintains a robust Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) / Anti-Money Laundering (AML) program. Strategically, the data aggregated in this table allows Risk Management to monitor alert volumes, refine matching algorithms to reduce false positives, and instantly adapt to newly published sanctions lists. This proactive stance ensures zero compliance violations in this critical area, safeguarding the lender's license to operate and protecting the enterprise from existential legal threats.
-- KPIs: OFAC scan completion rate, False positive rate, Sanctioned entity intercept rate, Scan latency, Audit finding resolution time
-- Feature Reference: F-29, F-139
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.ofac_scan_log (
    -- Primary key
    ofac_scan_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    borrower_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Scan details
    scan_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (scan_status IN ('CLEAR', 'POTENTIAL_MATCH', 'CONFIRMED_MATCH', 'ERROR', 'PENDING')),
    scan_type VARCHAR(50) CHECK (scan_type IN ('INITIAL', 'PERIODIC', 'MANUAL_REVIEW')),

    -- List version
    list_version VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    list_checked_date DATE NOT NULL,

    -- Match details
    match_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    match_entities JSONB,
    match_aliases JSONB,

    -- Risk scoring
    risk_score NUMERIC(5,2) CHECK (risk_score >= 0 AND risk_score <= 100),
    risk_level VARCHAR(20) CHECK (risk_level IN ('LOW', 'MEDIUM', 'HIGH', 'CRITICAL')),

    -- Review
    reviewed_by UUID,
    reviewed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    review_notes TEXT,

    -- Status
    is_clear BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_ofac_scan_log_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
        REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT ofac_scan_log_status_check CHECK (
        (scan_status = 'CLEAR' AND is_clear = TRUE) OR
        (scan_status != 'CLEAR' AND is_clear = FALSE)
    )
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.ofac_scan_log IS 'Logs OFAC/sanctions list checks against borrower data at POS entry, enabling BSA/AML compliance';

-- Indexes for ofac_scan_log table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_borrower ON pos.ofac_scan_log (borrower_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_scan_status ON pos.ofac_scan_log (scan_status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_risk_level ON pos.ofac_scan_log (risk_level);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_is_clear ON pos.ofac_scan_log (is_clear);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_created_at ON pos.ofac_scan_log (created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ofac_scan_log_list_checked_date ON pos.ofac_scan_log (list_checked_date);

-- TABLE: DB79 - view_audit_watermark
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB79 - view_audit_watermark
-- Description: Timestamps and IP logs capturing exact moments a borrower views specific disclosures
-- Business Case: The `view_audit_watermark` table captures the exact digital footprint of a borrower viewing specific disclosure documents within the POS portal, serving as the electronic equivalent of a certified mail receipt. It logs the document ID, the timestamp the document was rendered on the borrower's screen, the borrower's IP address, and the browser user-agent. Unlike eSignature, which tracks explicit consent, this table tracks passive consumption—proving that the borrower had the opportunity to read the material. Under TRID, certain waiting periods (e.g., the 3-day waiting period after the Loan Estimate is delivered) begin only when the borrower has received the disclosure. If eDelivery is used, this table provides the immutable, timestamped proof required to start the clock. It integrates with the disclosure package workflow, automatically updating the loan milestone status when a view is registered, and preventing the system from allowing the loan to proceed to closing prematurely.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `view_audit_watermark` table is eliminating regulatory ambiguity around eDelivery and accelerating the loan closing timeline. Without irrefutable proof that a borrower viewed a disclosure, lenders must wait for physical mail delivery confirmation, adding 3-7 days to the cycle. By capturing granular, forensic-level view data, Hyperion allows lenders to confidently rely on eDelivery, legally starting TRID waiting periods the instant the borrower opens the document. This directly achieves the 3x faster application-to-close time. Furthermore, in the event of a regulatory audit or borrower dispute ("I never saw that disclosure"), this table provides the exact IP address and timestamp needed to prove compliance, protecting the lender from CFPB fines and lawsuit liabilities. Strategically, analyzing view latency (how long after delivery the borrower actually opens the doc) allows the system to trigger proactive follow-up notifications, ensuring that waiting periods expire as fast as legally possible.
-- KPIs: eDelivery view confirmation rate, Time from delivery to view, TRID waiting period accuracy, Audit dispute resolution success rate, Physical mail volume reduction
-- Feature Reference: F-140
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.view_audit_watermark (
    -- Primary key
    view_audit_watermark_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    disclosure_package_id UUID NOT NULL,
    borrower_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- View details
    viewed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    viewed_ip INET NOT NULL,
    viewed_user_agent TEXT,

    -- Document context
    document_type VARCHAR(100),
    page_count INTEGER,
    view_duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (view_duration_seconds >= 0),

    -- View method
    view_method VARCHAR(20) CHECK (view_method IN ('PORTAL_VIEW', 'EMAIL_VIEW', 'SMS_VIEW', 'PRINT_VIEW')),

    -- Status
    is_acknowledged BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    acknowledged_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_view_audit_watermark_package FOREIGN KEY (disclosure_package_id)
        REFERENCES pos.disclosure_package(disclosure_package_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_view_audit_watermark_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
        REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.view_audit_watermark IS 'Timestamps and IP logs capturing exact moments a borrower views specific disclosures, enabling TRID compliance and eDelivery tracking';

-- Indexes for view_audit_watermark table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_package ON pos.view_audit_watermark (disclosure_package_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_borrower ON pos.view_audit_watermark (borrower_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_viewed_at ON pos.view_audit_watermark (viewed_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_viewed_ip ON pos.view_audit_watermark (viewed_ip);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_view_method ON pos.view_audit_watermark (view_method);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_view_audit_watermark_is_acknowledged ON pos.view_audit_watermark (is_acknowledged);

-- Table: DB80 - chat_attachment
-- Description: Stores files shared within the in-app secure chat
-- Business Case: The `chat_attachment` table stores the metadata and secure reference paths for files exchanged within the POS's native, secure chat interface. It captures the associated message ID, the file storage path, the original filename, and the file type (e.g., PDF, JPEG). This table ensures that documents shared between the borrower and the Loan Officer—such as a quick photo of a W-2 taken via mobile—are immediately indexed and securely stored within the loan's eFolder, rather than being lost in external email threads. It enforces file type and size validation, rejecting executable files to prevent malware injection. By linking attachments directly to the chat message context, it preserves the narrative of the loan file; an underwriter reviewing the chat history can see exactly what document was sent in response to a specific query, providing a complete, contextual audit trail that disconnected email inboxes cannot provide.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `chat_attachment` table is securing the communication channel, preventing PII leaks, and maintaining the contextual integrity of loan documentation. Currently, borrowers frequently email sensitive documents to their LOs using unsecured personal email accounts, creating massive SOC 2 / ISO 27001 violations and exposing the lender to data breaches. By forcing all file transfers into the secure, encrypted chat environment governed by this table, Hyperion eliminates the risk of PII interception. Operationally, capturing these files directly into the eFolder saves processors from the manual task of downloading attachments from Outlook and uploading them into the LOS, eliminating dual data entry and saving hours per loan. Strategically, this structured approach ensures that every piece of data relevant to the loan decision is captured within the unified data fabric, making the file fully auditable and protecting the lender from repurchase demands arising from missing documentation.
-- KPIs: Secure file transfer adoption rate, PII leakage incident reduction, Chat-to-eFolder auto-indexing accuracy, Malware intercept rate, Processor manual file handling time reduction
-- Feature Reference: F-23
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.chat_attachment (
    -- Primary key
    chat_attachment_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    chat_message_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- File details
    original_filename VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    storage_file_path VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    file_size_bytes BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (file_size_bytes >= 0),
    file_mime_type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    file_hash VARCHAR(64),

    -- File type
    file_category VARCHAR(50) CHECK (file_category IN ('DOCUMENT', 'IMAGE', 'SPREADSHEET', 'OTHER')),

    -- Security
    is_encrypted BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    encryption_key_hash VARCHAR(64),

    -- Status
    is_accessible BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    is_deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,

    -- Audit trail
    uploaded_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_chat_attachment_message FOREIGN KEY (chat_message_id)
        REFERENCES pos.chat_message(chat_message_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT chat_attachment_file_type_check CHECK (
        file_mime_type IN ('application/pdf', 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/tiff', 'application/vnd.ms-excel', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet', 'application/msword', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document')
    )
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.chat_attachment IS 'Stores files shared within the in-app secure chat, enabling secure document transfer and contextual eFolder integration';

-- Description: Stores templates for dynamic document generation (disclosures, LE)
-- Business Case: The `document_template` table is the central repository for the dynamic HTML and text templates used to generate all disclosure documents, loan estimates, and compliance notices within the POS. It stores the template content, the associated document type, the state applicability, and the version number. This table separates the presentation logic from the application data, allowing the system to merge borrower data into a compliant, formatted document on the fly. It also supports version control; when a template is updated, a new version is created, ensuring that historical loans retain the exact language of the document they signed, while new loans use the latest compliant version.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `document_template` table is eliminating the immense IT bottleneck and legal risk associated with generating compliant mortgage documents. In legacy architectures, document generation is hard-coded, meaning that a simple change to a state disclosure clause requires a software release cycle that can take weeks, leaving the lender exposed to compliance violations in the interim. By externalizing the templates into a managed database table, Hyperion allows compliance officers to make instant, point-and-click updates, achieving the Self-Learning Compliance Engine's goal of adapting to regulatory changes within hours. Operationally, this drastically reduces the cost of compliance maintenance. Strategically, the dynamic merging capability ensures that every document produced is a perfect, auditable reflection of the data in the unified fabric at the exact moment of generation, providing an ironclad defense against TRID tolerance and document fraud claims.

In traditional workflows, POA handling is largely manual, relying on processors to visually inspect complex legal documents, often leading to missed expirations or exceeded scopes of authority. By structuring POA data and feeding it to the AI Core for validation, Hyperion drastically reduces the chance of a closing error. Strategically, this table ensures that the "zero-touch" loan vision can accommodate complex edge cases like deployed military personnel or incapacitated borrowers without introducing manual bottlenecks or compliance risk, protecting the lender's capital and ensuring a frictionless closing.

Traditional systems cannot map these complex relationships, forcing processors to build offline spreadsheets, leading to a 25% rework rate and massive repurchase risk if ineligible funds are used. By structuring these relationships, Hyperion automates the asset verification process, instantly calculating true liquidity. This capability allows lenders to confidently serve the lucrative jumbo and non-QM markets, driving top-line revenue while maintaining CMMI Level 5 audit readiness.

By explicitly structuring this data, Hyperion guarantees that pricing and eligibility are calculated perfectly from the first click. Strategically, this allows lenders to confidently offer family-assist programs (like FHA loans with non-occupant co-borrowers) which are a massive growth market, knowing their risk is mathematically quantified and priced.

It supports intelligent routing—for example, routing a VOE request for a government employee directly to a specialized provider, while sending retail employees to a general database. The table also logs SLA metrics and cost per transaction, allowing the system to dynamically route to the fastest or most cost-effective provider in real-time.

By abstracting the configuration, Hyperion allows lenders to swap or add vendors in days, not months, leveraging competitive pricing. Strategically, the dynamic routing capability ensures that if Provider A is experiencing high latency, the system automatically fails over to Provider B, ensuring zero disruption to the borrower experience. This agility is a core pillar of the 50-year vision, ensuring the platform can seamlessly adapt as the open-banking and payroll API landscape evolves.

-- Table: DB107 - dependent_care_expense
-- Description: Tracks child care or elderly care expenses affecting DTI
-- Business Case: The `dependent_care_expense` table captures the monthly costs associated with caring for dependents (children or elderly parents) declared by the borrower. It stores the expense type, the monthly payment amount, and links directly to the `dependent` and `borrower` tables. This table is a critical input for the real-time Debt-to-Income (DTI) calculation engine. Under GSE guidelines, documented dependent care expenses that are not reimbursed must be included as a liability in the DTI ratio, as they represent a continuous, fixed reduction in available income. By structuring this data explicitly, the POS can prompt borrowers for this information contextually (only if dependents are declared) and automatically adjust the DTI logic, ensuring that the AUS submission reflects the borrower's true financial capacity without manual underwriter intervention.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `dependent_care_expense` table is ensuring precise underwriting calculations and preventing early payment default due to overstated borrower capacity. In traditional workflows, dependent care expenses are often missed during the initial application and only discovered by the underwriter weeks later, forcing a recalculation of the DTI that can kill the loan at the 11th hour. By capturing and structuring this data at the POS, Hyperion ensures real-time, accurate DTI feedback, preventing borrower disappointment and rework. Strategically, this level of granular, structured data feeds the AI fraud detection models, identifying anomalies where declared expenses seem too low for the number of dependents, thereby protecting the lender from misrepresented liabilities and ensuring zero compliance violations.
-- KPIs: Dependent expense capture rate, DTI calculation accuracy, Loan denial rate due to hidden liabilities, Underwriter DTI override rate, Data validation pass rate
-- Feature Reference: F-83
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.dependent_care_expense (

    monthly_amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (monthly_amount >= 0),
    provider_name VARCHAR(255),
    provider_contact_phone VARCHAR(20),

    -- Payment details
    payment_frequency VARCHAR(20) CHECK (payment_frequency IN ('MONTHLY', 'WEEKLY', 'BI_WEEKLY', 'QUARTERLY')),
    payment_method VARCHAR(50) CHECK (payment_method IN ('CASH', 'CHECK', 'ACH', 'CREDIT_CARD')),

    verification_document_upload_id UUID,

    -- Employer reimbursement
    is_employer_reimbursed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    employer_reimbursement_amount NUMERIC(12,2) CHECK (employer_reimbursement_amount >= 0),
    employer_reimbursement_verification_id UUID,

    CONSTRAINT dependent_care_expense_reimbursement_check CHECK (
        NOT is_employer_reimbursed OR employer_reimbursement_amount <= monthly_amount
    )
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.dependent_care_expense IS 'Tracks child care or elderly care expenses affecting DTI, enabling accurate underwriting calculations';

It supports the Self-Learning Compliance Engine by allowing regulatory updates regarding DPA guidelines to be deployed in hours. -- Business Case: The business case for the `dpa_program` table is democratizing homeownership by unlocking billions in unused government subsidies, thereby massively expanding the lender's eligible borrower pool. Down payment is the #1 barrier to homeownership, yet DPA programs are notoriously difficult for LOs to track, leading to missed opportunities and abandoned applications. By maintaining a real-time, structured catalog of DPA programs, Hyperion empowers the POS to proactively match borrowers with free capital at the point of sale, increasing conversion rates and driving loan volume. Strategically, this capability positions the lender as a community-focused, affordable housing leader, driving brand loyalty and opening avenues for Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) credits, while ensuring zero compliance violations regarding ineligible program combinations.
-- KPIs: DPA program match rate, DPA-assisted loan volume, Program data refresh frequency, Borrower conversion rate via DPA, CRA credit generation
-- Feature Reference: F-144
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.dpa_program (
    -- Primary key
    dpa_program_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Program identification
    program_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    program_code VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE,
    administering_agency VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

    -- Geographic scope
    state VARCHAR(2),
    region VARCHAR(100),
    county VARCHAR(100),
    city VARCHAR(100),

    -- Eligibility criteria
    max_income_limit NUMERIC(18,2),
    income_limit_percent_of_ami NUMERIC(5,2),
    max_purchase_price NUMERIC(18,2),
    min_credit_score INTEGER CHECK (min_credit_score >= 300 AND min_credit_score <= 850),
    max_loan_amount NUMERIC(18,2),

    -- Loan program compatibility
    eligible_loan_types TEXT[],

    -- Program details

    assistance_type VARCHAR(50) CHECK (assistance_type IN ('GRANT', 'SECOND_LIEN', 'FORGIVABLE_LOAN', 'DEFERRED_LOAN', 'DOWN_PAYMENT')),
    is_repayable BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    repayment_terms TEXT,

    -- Status

    expiration_date DATE,

    -- Application requirements

    application_deadline DATE,

    program_contact_email VARCHAR(255),
    program_website VARCHAR(255),

    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    created_by UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints

);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.dpa_program IS 'Reference table for Down Payment Assistance programs and criteria, enabling automated matching and compliance';

-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB111 - rental_income_calc
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB111 - rental_income_calc
-- Description: Stores the calculated net rental income for investment properties
-- Business Case: The `rental_income_calc` table stores the precise, system-calculated Net Rental Income used for qualifying the borrower, adhering strictly to GSE (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac) algorithms. It captures the gross rent, the specific vacancy factor applied (typically 25%), operating expenses, and the resulting net figure. It also stores the calculation method used (e.g., Schedule E, Lease Agreement). This table is populated by the AI Core, which extracts lease data from uploaded documents and applies the correct underwriting formula. It links directly to the property and the DTI calculation engine, ensuring that the impact of rental income on the borrower's debt ratio is mathematically perfect. If the borrower updates the lease amount, this table recalculates the net figure in real-time and instantly updates the DTI, providing immediate feedback to the borrower and LO without requiring an underwriter to manually recalculate on a scratchpad.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `rental_income_calc` table is eliminating the massive error rate and repurchase risk associated with the manual calculation of rental income. GSE guidelines for calculating net rental income are complex and frequently change; applying the wrong vacancy factor or failing to account for property taxes can drastically alter the borrower's DTI, leading to incorrect approvals and subsequent investor repurchase demands. By codifying the calculation into an automated, structured table, Hyperion guarantees 100% mathematical accuracy and GSE compliance. Strategically, the real-time recalculation capability empowers LOs to accurately advise real estate investors on the exact rent they need to charge to qualify for the loan, transforming the POS into a strategic advisory tool that closes more loans.
-- KPIs: Rental income calculation accuracy, Underwriter override rate, Repurchase rate due to income calc errors, Time to calculate net rent, Investment property pull-through rate
-- Feature Reference: F-88
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.rental_income_calc (
    -- Primary key
    rental_income_calc_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    property_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Input data
    gross_rent NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (gross_rent >= 0),
    vacancy_factor NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 25.0 CHECK (vacancy_factor >= 0 AND vacancy_factor <= 100),
    vacancy_amount NUMERIC(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gross_rent * vacancy_factor / 100) STORED,

    -- Expenses
    property_taxes NUMERIC(12,2),
    property_insurance NUMERIC(12,2),
    management_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
    maintenance_reserve NUMERIC(12,2),
    other_expenses NUMERIC(12,2),
    total_expenses NUMERIC(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        COALESCE(property_taxes, 0) + COALESCE(property_insurance, 0) +
        COALESCE(management_fees, 0) + COALESCE(maintenance_reserve, 0) +
        COALESCE(other_expenses, 0)
    ) STORED,

    -- Net income
    net_rental_income NUMERIC(12,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        gross_rent - (gross_rent * vacancy_factor / 100) - total_expenses
    ) STORED,

    -- Calculation details
    calculation_method VARCHAR(50) CHECK (calculation_method IN ('SCHEDULE_E', 'LEASE_AGREEMENT', 'GSE_FORM_1037', 'MANUAL')),
    calculation_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Verification
    verification_status pos.typ_verification_status_enum DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    verification_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    verification_notes TEXT,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_rental_income_calc_property FOREIGN KEY (property_id)
        REFERENCES pos.property(property_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT rental_income_calc_net_check CHECK (net_rental_income >= 0)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.rental_income_calc IS 'Stores the calculated net rental income for investment properties, enabling accurate DTI calculation';

-- Indexes for rental_income_calc table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rental_income_calc_property ON pos.rental_income_calc (property_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rental_income_calc_net_income ON pos.rental_income_calc (net_rental_income);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rental_income_calc_verification_status ON pos.rental_income_calc (verification_status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rental_income_calc_calculation_method ON pos.rental_income_calc (calculation_method);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rental_income_calc_calculation_date ON pos.rental_income_calc (calculation_date);

-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB115 - field_level_esign_req
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB115 - field_level_esign_req
-- Description: Defines which specific data field changes trigger a new eSignature
-- Business Case: The `field_level_esign_req` table defines the exact data tolerance thresholds that trigger a new eSignature requirement under TRID and E-SIGN regulations. It stores the field name (e.g., Loan Amount, Interest Rate), the variance threshold (e.g., 0% for rate, $100 for fees), and the required action (e.g., "Initial here"). This table acts as the compliance brain for the `field_change_history` table. If a borrower's income is updated after initial disclosures are signed, the system queries this table to determine if that specific change invalidates the prior consent. If it does, the table triggers an automated task for the borrower to re-sign the specific section using the field-level eSign feature. By externalizing these rules, compliance officers can adjust trigger thresholds in real-time as CFPB interpretations evolve, without requiring software updates.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `field_level_esign_req` table is preventing TRID tolerance violations and ensuring the legal enforceability of the digital mortgage contract. In traditional workflows, tracking which data changes require re-signing is a manual, error-prone process; missing a re-signature can render the loan unenforceable or expose the lender to fines. By automating the trigger logic, Hyperion guarantees that 100% of material changes are captured and consented to, reducing audit preparation time by 95%. Strategically, this table allows the platform to offer a highly granular, user-friendly eSign experience—asking borrowers to initial only the changed fields rather than forcing them to re-sign a 100-page package, which drastically reduces borrower abandonment at the re-disclosure stage.
-- KPIs: Re-signature trigger accuracy, TRID tolerance violation rate, Borrower re-signature completion rate, Compliance audit pass rate, Time to execute re-disclosure
-- Feature Reference: F-98
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.field_level_esign_req (
    -- Primary key
    field_level_esign_req_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Field identification
    field_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    table_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,

    -- Trigger thresholds
    variance_threshold_type VARCHAR(20) CHECK (variance_threshold_type IN ('PERCENTAGE', 'ABSOLUTE', 'EXACT_MATCH')),
    variance_threshold NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (variance_threshold >= 0),
    trigger_logic VARCHAR(50) CHECK (trigger_logic IN ('GREATER_THAN', 'GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL', 'EXACT_CHANGE')),

    -- Action required
    action_required VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    esign_category VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (esign_category IN ('DISCLOSURE', 'LOAN_AMOUNT', 'INTEREST_RATE', 'BORROWER_INFO', 'PROPERTY_INFO', 'INCOME', 'ASSETS')),

    -- Exemptions
    exemption_criteria JSONB,

    -- Status
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    is_mandatory BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    created_by UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT field_level_esign_req_unique UNIQUE (field_name, table_name)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.field_level_esign_req IS 'Defines which specific data field changes trigger a new eSignature, enabling TRID compliance and automated re-disclosure';

-- ====================================================================================
-- TABLE: DB117 - income_projection
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB117 - income_projection
-- Description: Stores YTD to Annual income projections for variable earners
-- Business Case: The `income_projection` table stores the AI-driven calculations used to annualize and project variable or self-employed income (e.g., hourly workers, gig economy, YTD base + commission). It captures the raw YTD amount, the projection method used (e.g., straight-line, trending, 24-month average), and the final qualifying annual figure. This table is critical for enforcing GSE income calculation guidelines programmatically. It links to the `employment` table, allowing the POS to present a transparent, real-time projection to the borrower. If the borrower uploads a new paystub, the AI extracts the new YTD total, recalculates the projection using the method defined in this table, and instantly updates the DTI. By storing the method alongside the result, it provides the underwriter with an immutable, explainable audit trail of how the income was derived.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `income_projection` table is accurately serving the growing gig and variable-income workforce, a massive segment that is routinely denied due to manual calculation errors. Traditional POS systems force borrowers to guess their annual income, which almost always conflicts with the underwriter's formal calculation, leading to loan denial and a 60% abandonment rate. By automating the projection using GSE-defined algorithms at the point of sale, Hyperion sets accurate expectations and ensures the loan is viable from day one. Strategically, the data captured here trains the AI to select the most advantageous calculation method for the borrower within GSE guidelines, acting as a digital advocate that maximizes loan volume while maintaining zero compliance risk.
-- KPIs: Variable income calculation accuracy, Underwriter override rate, Self-employed loan pull-through rate, Time to calculate annualized income, Income projection dispute rate
-- Feature Reference: F-145
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.income_projection (
    -- Primary key
    income_projection_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    employment_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Projection input
    ytd_income NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (ytd_income >= 0),
    ytd_months INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (ytd_months >= 1 AND ytd_months <= 12),
    monthly_average NUMERIC(18,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (ytd_income / ytd_months) STORED,

    -- Projection method
    projection_method VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (projection_method IN ('STRAIGHT_LINE', 'TRENDING', '12_MONTH_AVG', '24_MONTH_AVG', 'GSE_FORMULA')),
    projection_multiplier NUMERIC(10,2) DEFAULT 12,

    -- Projection result
    projected_annual_income NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL CHECK (projected_annual_income >= 0),
    projection_confidence NUMERIC(5,2) CHECK (projection_confidence >= 0 AND projection_confidence <= 100),

    -- Historical trend
    historical_trend JSONB,
    trend_direction VARCHAR(20) CHECK (trend_direction IN ('INCREASING', 'DECREASING', 'STABLE', 'VOLATILE')),

    -- Calculation details
    calculation_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    calculated_by VARCHAR(50) CHECK (calculated_by IN ('AI', 'MANUAL', 'SYSTEM')),

    -- Verification
    verification_status pos.typ_verification_status_enum DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    verification_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_income_projection_employment FOREIGN KEY (employment_id)
        REFERENCES pos.employment(employment_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.income_projection IS 'Stores YTD to Annual income projections for variable earners, enabling accurate underwriting for non-traditional income';

-- Indexes for income_projection table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_income_projection_employment ON pos.income_projection (employment_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_income_projection_projection_method ON pos.income_projection (projection_method);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_income_projection_verification_status ON pos.income_projection (verification_status);

-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB118 - rate_lock_request
-- Description: Logs borrower-initiated rate lock requests from the POS
-- Business Case: The `rate_lock_request` table logs the specific moment a borrower or Loan Officer initiates a request to lock the interest rate within the POS. It captures the requested rate, the lock duration (e.g., 30, 45, 60 days), the requested margin, and the status of the request (pending, approved, expired). This table acts as the bridge between the consumer-facing POS and the capital markets desk. When a borrower clicks "Lock Rate," this table records the event and pushes an alert to the lock desk via the webhook engine. It timestamps the request to the millisecond, ensuring that if market rates shift during the approval process, the lender has a forensic record of the exact time the lock was requested, protecting them from rate volatility disputes.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `rate_lock_request` table is empowering borrowers with real-time control over their rate while providing the secondary market desk with the instant visibility required to hedge pipeline risk. In traditional workflows, rate locks are handled via email or phone calls between the LO and the desk, a process that introduces latency, errors, and missed opportunities. By structuring the request within the POS, Hyperion ensures zero data re-entry and accelerates the lock confirmation time from hours to minutes. Strategically, capturing the exact timestamp and terms of the request is vital for compliance and profitability; it ensures the lender can honor the borrower's rate even if the market moves, while protecting the desk from fallout risk.
-- KPIs: Rate lock request latency, Lock confirmation turnaround time, Lock fallout rate, Secondary market sync accuracy, Borrower lock abandonment rate
-- Feature Reference: F-146
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.rate_lock_request (
    -- Primary key
    rate_lock_request_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Lock details
    requested_rate NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL CHECK (requested_rate >= 0 AND requested_rate <= 100),
    requested_lock_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (requested_lock_days IN (15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120)),
    requested_margin NUMERIC(7,4),

    -- Lender response
    approved_rate NUMERIC(7,4),
    approved_lock_days INTEGER,
    approval_reference VARCHAR(100),

    -- Status
    lock_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING' CHECK (lock_status IN ('PENDING', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', 'EXPIRED', 'CANCELLED')),
    status_reason TEXT,

    -- Timestamps
    requested_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    rejected_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Borrower context
    requested_by UUID NOT NULL,
    requested_by_role VARCHAR(50) CHECK (requested_by_role IN ('BORROWER', 'LOAN_OFFICER')),

    -- Market context
    market_rate_at_request NUMERIC(7,4),
    rate_spread NUMERIC(7,4),

    -- Webhook tracking
    webhook_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    webhook_response JSONB,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_request_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.rate_lock_request IS 'Logs borrower-initiated rate lock requests from the POS, enabling real-time rate locking and secondary market sync';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rate_lock_request_lock_status ON pos.rate_lock_request (lock_status);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rate_lock_request_expires_at ON pos.rate_lock_request (expires_at);

-- TABLE: DB121 - appointment_slot
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB121 - appointment_slot
-- Description: Available calendly-style slots for LO appointments
-- Business Case: The `appointment_slot` table manages the availability calendar for Loan Officers and field agents directly within the POS ecosystem. It stores the user ID of the LO, the start time, end time, and the booking status (available, booked, blocked). This table replaces the need for external scheduling tools like Calendly by natively integrating calendar availability with the loan application flow. It ensures that a borrower requesting an appointment is only presented with times that the LO is actually available, considering time zones and working hours. It supports dynamic availability, automatically blocking out slots when an LO's pipeline is full, or opening up slots based on real-time staffing. By centralizing scheduling, it ensures that the appointment data is linked directly to the borrower's session and application.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `appointment_slot` table is eliminating the "phone tag" and scheduling friction that causes massive lead leakage at the top of the funnel. When a borrower is ready to talk, forcing them to exchange multiple emails to find a mutually available time drastically increases the chance they will abandon the process or move to a competitor. By offering a self-service, native booking system, Hyperion connects the borrower to the LO instantly, maximizing conversion rates. Strategically, the data captured here allows sales managers to analyze LO availability and capacity, ensuring that lead distribution is balanced and that top producers aren't overbooked, optimizing the efficiency of the human sales force.
-- KPIs: Appointment booking completion rate, Time from lead to appointment, No-show rate, LO calendar utilization, Lead leakage due to scheduling friction
-- Feature Reference: F-53
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.appointment_slot (
    -- Primary key
    appointment_slot_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- LO identification
    lo_user_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Time details
    start_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    end_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    timezone VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'America/New_York',

    -- Availability
    is_available BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    is_booked BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    is_blocked BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    block_reason TEXT,

    -- Booking details
    booked_by UUID,
    booked_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    booking_reference VARCHAR(100),

    -- Slot type
    slot_type VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'CONSULTATION' CHECK (slot_type IN ('CONSULTATION', 'DOCUMENT_REVIEW', 'CLOSING', 'DISCLOSURE_REVIEW', 'OTHER')),
    slot_duration_minutes INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (end_time - start_time)) / 60) STORED,

    -- Status
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'AVAILABLE' CHECK (status IN ('AVAILABLE', 'BOOKED', 'BLOCKED', 'CANCELLED', 'COMPLETED', 'NO_SHOW')),

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    created_by UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT appointment_slot_dates_check CHECK (end_time > start_time)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.appointment_slot IS 'Available calendly-style slots for LO appointments, enabling native scheduling and reduced lead friction';

-- Indexes for appointment_slot table

-- TABLE: DB122 - appointment_booking
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB122 - appointment_booking
-- Description: Tracks borrower bookings of LO time slots
-- Business Case: The `appointment_booking` table records the specific details of a scheduled meeting between a borrower and a Loan Officer. It links the `appointment_slot` ID, the borrower ID, and the application ID. It captures the meeting type (e.g., initial consultation, document review), the location (Zoom link, physical branch), and the status (scheduled, completed, canceled). This table acts as the operational log of the sales process. Once a booking is made, it triggers the Notification Engine to send calendar invites and automated reminders to both parties, reducing no-shows. If the borrower cancels, the table automatically releases the `appointment_slot` back to the available pool. It provides a complete audit trail of the borrower-LO interaction timeline, which is essential for compliance and sales management.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `appointment_booking` table is ensuring that scheduled leads actually result in funded loans through automated follow-up and reduced no-show rates. A booked appointment is not a closed loan; without structured tracking and automated reminders, no-show rates can exceed 30%, wasting LO time and killing pipeline velocity. By managing the booking lifecycle within the data fabric, Hyperion ensures that automated reminders are triggered, drastically reducing no-shows. Strategically, the data links the booking event to the final loan outcome, allowing executives to calculate the exact ROI of an LO's time and identify which types of appointments yield the highest conversion rates, enabling continuous optimization of the sales process.
-- KPIs: Booking-to-show rate, Post-appointment application conversion rate, No-show reduction rate, Cancellation re-booking rate, Time from booking to application start
-- Feature Reference: F-53
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.appointment_booking (
    -- Primary key
    appointment_booking_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    appointment_slot_id UUID NOT NULL,
    borrower_id UUID NOT NULL,
    application_id UUID,

    -- Meeting details
    meeting_type VARCHAR(50) CHECK (meeting_type IN ('INITIAL_CONSULTATION', 'DOCUMENT_REVIEW', 'DISCLOSURE_WALKTHROUGH', 'CLOSING', 'FOLLOW_UP')),
    meeting_location VARCHAR(255),
    meeting_link VARCHAR(500),
    meeting_notes TEXT,

    -- Booking details
    booked_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    booked_by UUID NOT NULL,
    booking_source VARCHAR(50) CHECK (booking_source IN ('PORTAL', 'LO_INITIATED', 'BORROWER_INITIATED', 'SYSTEM')),

    -- Status
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'SCHEDULED' CHECK (status IN ('SCHEDULED', 'COMPLETED', 'CANCELLED', 'NO_SHOW', 'RESCHEDULED')),
    status_reason TEXT,

    -- Timestamps
    scheduled_start TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    scheduled_end TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    actual_start TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    actual_end TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Reminders
    reminder_sent_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    reminder_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,

    -- No-show tracking
    is_no_show BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    no_show_reason TEXT,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_appointment_booking_slot FOREIGN KEY (appointment_slot_id)
        REFERENCES pos.appointment_slot(appointment_slot_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_appointment_booking_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
        REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_appointment_booking_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    CONSTRAINT appointment_booking_dates_check CHECK (scheduled_end > scheduled_start)
);
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.appointment_booking IS 'Tracks borrower bookings of LO time slots, enabling sales process tracking and no-show reduction';
