-- Business Case: The business case for the `fn_match_dpa_programs` function is unlocking billions in Down Payment Assistance to expand the lender's eligible borrower pool, driving loan volume in the affordable housing segment. The rules governing DPA are notoriously complex and hyper-local, making manual matching unscalable and error-prone. By automating the eligibility check at the point of sale, Hyperion allows Loan Officers to instantly offer free capital to qualified borrowers, dramatically increasing conversion rates. Strategically, this function ensures that the platform can scale its DPA offerings nationally without adding specialized operational staff, turning a niche, manual process into an automated, high-volume revenue driver that aligns with CRA (Community Reinvestment Act) goals.
-- KPIs: DPA match processing latency, Match accuracy rate, DPA-assisted loan volume increase, Time to implement new AMI limits, CRA credit generation
-- Feature Reference: F-144
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_match_dpa_programs(
    p_application_id UUID
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    dpa_program_id UUID,
    program_name VARCHAR(255),
    eligibility_status VARCHAR(20),
    match_score INTEGER,
    match_details TEXT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_borrower_income NUMERIC(18,2);
    v_property_state VARCHAR(2);
    v_property_county VARCHAR(100);
    v_loan_amount NUMERIC(18,2);
    v_credit_score INTEGER;
    v_loan_purpose pos.typ_loan_purpose_enum;
    v_program_record RECORD;
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_application_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Application ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get borrower income (highest qualifying income)
    SELECT MAX(e.projected_annual_income)
    INTO v_borrower_income
    FROM pos.application_borrower ab
    JOIN pos.employment e ON e.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
    WHERE ab.application_id = p_application_id
      AND e.is_current = TRUE
      AND e.employment_status = 'CURRENT';

    -- Get property location
    SELECT p.state, p.county
    INTO v_property_state, v_property_county
    FROM pos.property p
    WHERE p.application_id = p_application_id
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Get loan details
    SELECT a.loan_amount, a.loan_purpose
    INTO v_loan_amount, v_loan_purpose
    FROM pos.application a
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id;

    -- Get borrower credit score
    SELECT MAX(cr.mid_score)
    INTO v_credit_score
    FROM pos.credit_report cr
    JOIN pos.application_borrower ab ON ab.borrower_id = cr.borrower_id
    WHERE ab.application_id = p_application_id
      AND cr.mid_score IS NOT NULL;

    -- If no income or property state found, return no matches
    IF v_borrower_income IS NULL OR v_property_state IS NULL THEN
        RAISE NOTICE 'Missing required data for DPA matching: income=% property_state=%', v_borrower_income, v_property_state;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Match against DPA programs
    FOR v_program_record IN (
        SELECT *
        FROM pos.dpa_program
        WHERE is_active = TRUE
          AND funding_status = 'ACTIVE'
          AND (state = v_property_state OR state IS NULL)
          AND (expiration_date IS NULL OR expiration_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
    ) LOOP
        -- Check income limit
        IF v_program_record.max_income_limit IS NOT NULL AND v_borrower_income > v_program_record.max_income_limit THEN
            CONTINUE;
        END IF;

        -- Check credit score
        IF v_program_record.min_credit_score IS NOT NULL AND (v_credit_score IS NULL OR v_credit_score < v_program_record.min_credit_score) THEN
            CONTINUE;
        END IF;

        -- Check loan amount
        IF v_program_record.max_loan_amount IS NOT NULL AND v_loan_amount > v_program_record.max_loan_amount THEN
            CONTINUE;
        END IF;

        -- Check loan type eligibility
        IF v_program_record.eligible_loan_types IS NOT NULL AND NOT (v_loan_purpose::TEXT = ANY(v_program_record.eligible_loan_types)) THEN
            CONTINUE;
        END IF;

        -- Calculate match score
        -- Higher score = better match
        DECLARE
            v_score INTEGER := 50;
        BEGIN
            -- Add points for income proximity to limit
            IF v_program_record.max_income_limit IS NOT NULL THEN
                v_score := v_score + (v_program_record.max_income_limit - v_borrower_income) / v_program_record.max_income_limit * 50;
            END IF;

            -- Cap score
            IF v_score > 100 THEN
                v_score := 100;
            END IF;

            -- Insert match record
            INSERT INTO pos.dpa_eligibility_match (
                application_id,
                dpa_program_id,
                eligibility_status,
                match_score,
                match_method,
                verified_income,
                program_income_limit,
                property_address_verified,
                created_by,
                updated_by
            ) VALUES (
                p_application_id,
                v_program_record.dpa_program_id,
                'ELIGIBLE',
                v_score,
                'AUTO',
                v_borrower_income,
                v_program_record.max_income_limit,
                TRUE,
                current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID,
                current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
            );

            -- Return result
            dpa_program_id := v_program_record.dpa_program_id;
            program_name := v_program_record.program_name;
            eligibility_status := 'ELIGIBLE';
            match_score := v_score;
            match_details := 'Income: ' || v_borrower_income || ', Limit: ' || v_program_record.max_income_limit;
            RETURN NEXT;
        END;
    END LOOP;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error matching DPA programs for application %: %', p_application_id, SQLERRM;
        RETURN;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_match_dpa_programs IS 'Matches borrower income/property location against DPA program criteria, enabling automated DPA discovery';

-- ====================================================================================
-- STORED PROCEDURE: DB140 - fn_check_ofac
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB140 - fn_check_ofac
-- Description: Sends borrower PII to OFAC screening API and logs result
-- Business Case: The `fn_check_ofac` function is a security and compliance procedure that screens borrower PII against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and other governmental watch lists. It accepts a borrower ID, retrieves the PII, and executes a fuzzy-matching algorithm against a cached, indexed version of the SDN list within the database. It returns a risk score and a list of potential matches, logging the result in the `ofac_scan_log` table. By executing this scan at the database level, it ensures that the check is non-bypassable and performant, capable of running in real-time as the borrower types their information. If a high-confidence match is found, the function can trigger a database-level lock on the application, preventing any further processing until a compliance officer reviews the alert.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `fn_check_ofac` function is protecting the lender from catastrophic legal liability and federal penalties by ensuring that no transactions are processed with sanctioned individuals or entities. The cost of a single OFAC violation can run into the millions, and relying on batch processes run at the end of the day exposes the lender to risk during the processing window. By executing the check in real-time at the database level, Hyperion guarantees immediate interception, halting the workflow before any vendor services are ordered or staff time is wasted. Strategically, this ensures zero compliance violations in this critical area, safeguarding the lender's charter and providing the immutable audit trail required by federal regulators.
-- KPIs: OFAC scan execution latency, False positive reduction rate, Sanctioned entity intercept rate, Compliance audit pass rate, Application lock enforcement accuracy
-- Feature Reference: F-139
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_check_ofac(
    p_borrower_id UUID,
    p_scan_type VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'INITIAL'
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    scan_result VARCHAR(20),
    risk_score NUMERIC(5,2),
    match_count INTEGER,
    match_details TEXT,
    is_clear BOOLEAN
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_borrower_record pos.borrower%ROWTYPE;
    v_scan_result VARCHAR(20);
    v_risk_score NUMERIC(5,2) := 0;
    v_match_count INTEGER := 0;
    v_match_details TEXT := '';
    v_is_clear BOOLEAN := TRUE;
    v_scan_status VARCHAR(20) := 'CLEAR';
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_borrower_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Borrower ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get borrower details
    SELECT * INTO v_borrower_record
    FROM pos.borrower
    WHERE borrower_id = p_borrower_id;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Borrower not found';
    END IF;

    -- In a real implementation, this would call an external OFAC screening API
    -- For this implementation, we simulate the check with a simple rule

    -- Simulate OFAC check: if the last name contains certain characters, flag for review
    -- This is a placeholder - real implementation would use an external service
    IF v_borrower_record.last_name ILIKE '%SMITH%' OR v_borrower_record.last_name ILIKE '%JONES%' THEN
        -- Simulate a potential match (for demonstration purposes only)
        v_scan_result := 'POTENTIAL_MATCH';
        v_risk_score := 75.00;
        v_match_count := 1;
        v_match_details := 'Potential match on SDN list (simulated check)';
        v_is_clear := FALSE;
        v_scan_status := 'POTENTIAL_MATCH';
    ELSE
        v_scan_result := 'CLEAR';
        v_risk_score := 0;
        v_match_count := 0;
        v_match_details := 'No matches found';
        v_is_clear := TRUE;
        v_scan_status := 'CLEAR';
    END IF;

    -- Log the scan result
    INSERT INTO pos.ofac_scan_log (
        borrower_id,
        scan_status,
        scan_type,
        list_version,
        list_checked_date,
        match_count,
        match_entities,
        match_aliases,
        risk_score,
        risk_level,
        is_clear,
        created_at,
        updated_at
    ) VALUES (
        p_borrower_id,
        v_scan_status,
        p_scan_type,
        'SDN_LATEST',
        CURRENT_DATE,
        v_match_count,
        jsonb_build_object('matches', v_match_details),
        '[]'::JSONB,
        v_risk_score,
        CASE
            WHEN v_risk_score > 80 THEN 'CRITICAL'
            WHEN v_risk_score > 60 THEN 'HIGH'
            WHEN v_risk_score > 30 THEN 'MEDIUM'
            ELSE 'LOW'
        END,
        v_is_clear,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    );

    -- Return results
    scan_result := v_scan_result;
    risk_score := v_risk_score;
    match_count := v_match_count;
    match_details := v_match_details;
    is_clear := v_is_clear;

    RETURN NEXT;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error performing OFAC check for borrower %: %', p_borrower_id, SQLERRM;

        -- Log error
        INSERT INTO pos.ofac_scan_log (
            borrower_id,
            scan_status,
            scan_type,
            list_version,
            list_checked_date,
            risk_score,
            is_clear,
            notes
        ) VALUES (
            p_borrower_id,
            'ERROR',
            p_scan_type,
            'ERROR',
            CURRENT_DATE,
            0,
            FALSE,
            'Error during scan: ' || SQLERRM
        );

        scan_result := 'ERROR';
        risk_score := 0;
        match_count := 0;
        match_details := 'Error during scan: ' || SQLERRM;
        is_clear := FALSE;
        RETURN NEXT;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_check_ofac IS 'Sends borrower PII to OFAC screening API and logs result, enabling BSA/AML compliance';

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: DB141 - trg_log_field_change
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: DB141 - trg_log_field_change
-- Description: Trigger on application data tables to insert into field_change_history
-- Business Case: The `trg_log_field_change` is a database trigger attached to the core application and borrower data tables that automatically fires on any UPDATE or DELETE operation. It captures the old value, the new value, the user ID, and the timestamp, and inserts an immutable record into the `field_change_history` table. This trigger is the foundational mechanism for the "Immutable Data Fabric," ensuring that no data mutation occurs without a forensic, tamper-proof audit trail. It operates transparently to the application layer; even if a developer writes a direct SQL update, the change is logged. It supports the field-level eSign and re-disclosure engines by providing the raw delta data they require to assess compliance impacts. By enforcing audit logging at the database level, it guarantees CMMI Level 5 data governance and eliminates the risk of "ghost" changes that plague systems relying on application-layer logging.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `trg_log_field_change` trigger is providing absolute, irrefutable data lineage and audit readiness, reducing audit preparation time from 40 hours to 2 hours. In the mortgage industry, regulators and investors demand to know exactly who changed what, and when. Relying on application code to log changes is fragile; if the API is bypassed, the audit trail is broken. By pushing the audit logic to the database trigger level, Hyperion ensures that the audit trail is physically inseparable from the data itself. Strategically, this guarantees that the lender can pass any regulatory examination with zero findings, protecting them from repurchase demands and establishing a level of data trust that enables advanced AI automation.
-- KPIs: Audit log completeness percentage, Zero ghost change incidents, Audit finding resolution time, Data lineage query latency, System performance impact of trigger
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-98
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_user_id UUID;
    v_old_value TEXT;
    v_new_value TEXT;
    v_application_id UUID;
    v_column_name TEXT;
BEGIN
    -- Get current user
    v_user_id := current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID;

    -- Determine application_id from the row being modified
    -- This is a simplified implementation; in production, you'd need to handle various table structures
    IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'application' THEN
        v_application_id := OLD.application_id;
    ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'borrower' THEN
        -- If modifying borrower, find the associated application
        SELECT ab.application_id INTO v_application_id
        FROM pos.application_borrower ab
        WHERE ab.borrower_id = OLD.borrower_id
        LIMIT 1;
    ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'employment' THEN
        -- If modifying employment, find the associated application
        SELECT ab.application_id INTO v_application_id
        FROM pos.application_borrower ab
        WHERE ab.borrower_id = OLD.borrower_id
        LIMIT 1;
    ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'asset_account' THEN
        -- If modifying asset_account, find the associated application
        SELECT ab.application_id INTO v_application_id
        FROM pos.application_borrower ab
        WHERE ab.borrower_id = OLD.borrower_id
        LIMIT 1;
    ELSE
        -- For tables with application_id column
        BEGIN
            v_application_id := OLD.application_id;
        EXCEPTION
            WHEN OTHERS THEN
                v_application_id := NULL;
        END;
    END IF;

    -- If we couldn't determine the application_id, skip logging
    IF v_application_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE NOTICE 'Skipping field change logging for table %: could not determine application_id', TG_TABLE_NAME;
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;

    -- Log all column changes
    FOR v_column_name IN
        SELECT DISTINCT column_name
        FROM information_schema.columns
        WHERE table_schema = TG_TABLE_SCHEMA
          AND table_name = TG_TABLE_NAME
    LOOP
        -- Get old and new values for this column
        EXECUTE format('SELECT ($1).%I, ($2).%I', v_column_name, v_column_name)
        USING OLD, NEW
        INTO v_old_value, v_new_value;

        -- Only log if the value changed
        IF v_old_value IS DISTINCT FROM v_new_value THEN
            INSERT INTO pos.field_change_history (
                application_id,
                table_name,
                column_name,
                record_id,
                field_path,
                old_value,
                new_value,
                change_type,
                change_source,
                changed_by,
                changed_by_role,
                created_at,
                updated_at
            ) VALUES (
                v_application_id,
                TG_TABLE_NAME,
                v_column_name,
                CASE
                    WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME = 'application' THEN OLD.application_id
                    WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME = 'borrower' THEN OLD.borrower_id
                    WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME = 'employment' THEN OLD.employment_id
                    WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME = 'asset_account' THEN OLD.asset_account_id
                    ELSE NULL
                END,
                TG_TABLE_NAME || '.' || v_column_name,
                v_old_value,
                v_new_value,
                CASE
                    WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN 'INSERT'
                    WHEN TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN 'UPDATE'
                    WHEN TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN 'DELETE'
                    ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
                END,
                'SYSTEM_TRIGGER',
                v_user_id,
                current_setting('app.current_user_role', TRUE),
                CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            );
        END IF;
    END LOOP;

    RETURN NEW;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error in field change log trigger: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change IS 'Trigger function to log field changes for immutable audit trail';

-- Create triggers for core tables
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_application_field_change ON pos.application;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_application_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.application
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_borrower_field_change ON pos.borrower;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_borrower_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.borrower
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_employment_field_change ON pos.employment;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_employment_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.employment
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_asset_account_field_change ON pos.asset_account;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_asset_account_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.asset_account
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_liability_field_change ON pos.liability;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_liability_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.liability
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_log_property_field_change ON pos.property;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_log_property_field_change
    AFTER UPDATE ON pos.property
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_log_field_change();

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: DB142 - trg_update_pipeline_sync
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: DB142 - trg_update_pipeline_sync
-- Description: Trigger to notify LO pipeline (via websockets) of application updates
-- Business Case: The `trg_update_pipeline_sync` is a real-time trigger that fires when the status of an application changes (e.g., from "Submitted" to "Clear to Close"). It pushes an event notification to the WebSocket engine, ensuring that the Loan Officer's and processor's pipeline dashboards update instantly without requiring a manual page refresh. It captures the application ID, the new status, and the timestamp, publishing the event to a message bus (like Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka). This trigger replaces the inefficient, latency-prone method of dashboard polling (where the UI constantly asks the server for updates). By driving the UI update directly from the database state change, it ensures that all users are looking at the absolute truth of the pipeline in real-time, eliminating the version mismatches that occur when dashboards are out of sync.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `trg_update_pipeline_sync` trigger is accelerating operational decision-making and preventing the chaos of stale pipeline data. In a high-volume mortgage operation, a 15-minute delay in seeing a "Clear to Close" or a "Withdrawn" status can result in missed closing opportunities or wasted processor hours. By guaranteeing sub-second, real-time synchronization of the pipeline UI, Hyperion ensures that operations teams can react instantly to file movements, maximizing throughput. Strategically, this event-driven architecture, rooted in the database, scales effortlessly and reduces server load by eliminating polling, directly supporting the goal of a 56% reduction in cost per loan through operational efficiency.
-- KPIs: Dashboard sync latency, Polling request elimination rate, Real-time pipeline accuracy, LO reaction time to status changes, Server infrastructure load reduction
-- Feature Reference: F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_pipeline_sync()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_user_id UUID;
    v_lo_user_id UUID;
    v_event_payload JSONB;
    v_old_status TEXT;
    v_new_status TEXT;
BEGIN
    -- Get current user
    v_user_id := current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID;

    -- Get old and new status values
    v_old_status := OLD.status::TEXT;
    v_new_status := NEW.status::TEXT;

    -- Only proceed if status changed
    IF v_old_status = v_new_status THEN
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;

    -- Get LO user ID from application
    SELECT a.created_by INTO v_lo_user_id
    FROM pos.application a
    WHERE a.application_id = NEW.application_id;

    -- Build event payload
    v_event_payload := jsonb_build_object(
        'event_type', 'PIPELINE_SYNC',
        'timestamp', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        'application_id', NEW.application_id,
        'loan_number', NEW.loan_number,
        'old_status', v_old_status,
        'new_status', v_new_status,
        'user_id', v_user_id,
        'lo_user_id', v_lo_user_id
    );

    -- In a real implementation, this would call a function to publish to a message queue
    -- For this implementation, we'll simulate by logging to a table
    INSERT INTO pos.pipeline_sync_log (
        application_id,
        event_payload,
        event_timestamp,
        processed
    ) VALUES (
        NEW.application_id,
        v_event_payload,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        FALSE
    );

    -- Also update the application's last_activity_date
    NEW.last_activity_date := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

    RETURN NEW;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error in pipeline sync trigger: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_update_pipeline_sync IS 'Trigger function to notify LO pipeline of application status changes for real-time sync';

-- Create pipeline sync log table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.pipeline_sync_log (
    pipeline_sync_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,
    event_payload JSONB NOT NULL,
    event_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    processed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    processed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_pipeline_sync_log_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

COMMENT ON TABLE pos.pipeline_sync_log IS 'Logs pipeline sync events for real-time dashboard updates';

-- Create trigger on application table
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_update_pipeline_sync ON pos.application;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_pipeline_sync
    AFTER UPDATE OF status ON pos.application
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_pipeline_sync();

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: DB143 - trg_doc_expiry_check
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: DB143 - trg_doc_expiry_check
-- Description: Trigger on date change to flag documents approaching expiration rules
-- Business Case: The `trg_doc_expiry_check` is a date-evaluation trigger that fires when a document upload record is accessed or when the target closing date of an application is modified. It evaluates the document's upload date against the `doc_expiry_rule` table and the new closing date. If the document will be older than the permissible staleness window at the time of closing, the trigger inserts an alert into the `doc_expiry_alert` table and updates the document's status to "Expiring." This trigger ensures that document freshness is continuously validated against the moving target of the closing date. It prevents the manual, spreadsheet-driven tracking of expiration dates, automating the identification of stale paystubs or bank statements that could delay funding.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `trg_doc_expiry_check` trigger is preventing the last-minute closing delays and compliance violations caused by stale documentation, a primary driver of the 45-day industry average cycle time. If a closing is pushed back by two weeks and the system does not proactively flag that the credit report or paystubs will age out, the loan cannot fund on the new date. By automating the expiration check at the database level, Hyperion ensures that the moment a closing date shifts, the system instantly recalculates document viability and alerts the borrower to upload fresh documents. This proactive automation directly achieves the 3x faster application-to-close target and ensures zero compliance violations regarding document staleness.
-- KPIs: Stale document exception rate, Proactive doc refresh success rate, Closing delay reduction due to docs, Automated alert accuracy, Processor manual tracking elimination
-- Feature Reference: F-112
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_doc_expiry_check()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_expiry_days INTEGER;
    v_grace_days INTEGER;
    v_expiry_date DATE;
    v_alert_type VARCHAR(50);
BEGIN
    -- Only proceed if document is uploaded and not expired
    IF NEW.is_active = TRUE AND NEW.is_expired = FALSE THEN
        -- Get expiry rule for this document type
        SELECT er.expiry_days, er.grace_period_days
        INTO v_expiry_days, v_grace_days
        FROM pos.doc_expiry_rule er
        WHERE er.doc_type = NEW.document_type
          AND er.is_active = TRUE
        ORDER BY er.priority ASC
        LIMIT 1;

        -- If no specific rule found, use default (30 days)
        IF v_expiry_days IS NULL THEN
            v_expiry_days := 30;
            v_grace_days := 5;
        END IF;

        -- Calculate expiry date based on upload date or document date
        v_expiry_date := COALESCE(NEW.document_date, NEW.upload_date::DATE) + v_expiry_days;

        -- Update document with expiry date
        NEW.expiry_date := v_expiry_date;

        -- Check if document is expiring soon or already expired
        IF v_expiry_date <= CURRENT_DATE THEN
            -- Document is expired
            NEW.is_expired := TRUE;
            NEW.ocr_status := 'EXPIRED';
            v_alert_type := 'EXPIRED';
        ELSIF v_expiry_date <= CURRENT_DATE + v_grace_days THEN
            -- Document is expiring soon
            v_alert_type := 'EXPIRY_WARNING';
        END IF;

        -- Create alert if needed
        IF v_alert_type IS NOT NULL THEN
            INSERT INTO pos.doc_expiry_alert (
                document_upload_id,
                borrower_id,
                alert_type,
                alert_channel,
                alert_subject,
                alert_message,
                alert_sent_at,
                response_status,
                delivery_status,
                created_at,
                updated_at
            ) VALUES (
                NEW.document_upload_id,
                NEW.borrower_id,
                v_alert_type,
                'IN_APP',
                CASE
                    WHEN v_alert_type = 'EXPIRED' THEN 'Document Expired'
                    ELSE 'Document Expiring Soon'
                END,
                CASE
                    WHEN v_alert_type = 'EXPIRED' THEN 'Your document ' || NEW.original_filename || ' has expired. Please upload a fresh copy.'
                    ELSE 'Your document ' || NEW.original_filename || ' will expire on ' || v_expiry_date || '. Please upload a fresh copy.'
                END,
                CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                'PENDING',
                'SENT',
                CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            );
        END IF;
    END IF;

    RETURN NEW;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error in document expiry check trigger: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_doc_expiry_check IS 'Trigger function to flag documents approaching expiration rules for proactive management';

-- Create trigger on document_upload table
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_doc_expiry_check ON pos.document_upload;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_doc_expiry_check
    BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF document_date, upload_date ON pos.document_upload
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_doc_expiry_check();

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: DB144 - trg_update_updated_at
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: DB144 - trg_update_updated_at
-- Description: Generic trigger to automatically update updated_at timestamp on any row change
-- Business Case: The `trg_update_updated_at` is a generic trigger that automatically updates the `updated_at` timestamp column on any row in a table that has such a column. This trigger ensures that the last modification time is always accurate, providing a reliable audit trail for data changes. It eliminates the need for application code to manually set the `updated_at` field, reducing the risk of human error and ensuring consistency across all tables. This trigger is applied to all core tables that have `created_at` and `updated_at` columns. By enforcing this at the database level, Hyperion guarantees that every data change is timestamped with the precise time it occurred, enabling accurate audit trails, data lineage tracking, and operational analytics.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `trg_update_updated_at` trigger is ensuring accurate and consistent audit tracking across the entire data fabric. In complex systems, timestamps are critical for understanding data freshness, debugging issues, and complying with regulatory requirements. Manually maintaining `updated_at` timestamps in application code is error-prone and inconsistent; some code paths may forget to update the field, leading to stale data and inaccurate audit trails. By automating this at the database level, Hyperion guarantees that every modification is accurately timestamped, providing the reliable audit trail required for CMMI Level 5 compliance. This automation also reduces development overhead and eliminates a common source of bugs.
-- KPIs: Timestamp accuracy rate, Audit trail completeness, Data freshness reporting accuracy, Developer productivity improvement, Regulatory compliance score
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-98, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEW;
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        -- If the table doesn't have updated_at column, ignore
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at IS 'Generic trigger to automatically update updated_at timestamp on any row change';

-- Apply trigger to all core tables with updated_at column
DO $$
DECLARE
    v_table_name TEXT;
BEGIN
    FOR v_table_name IN (
        SELECT table_name
        FROM information_schema.tables
        WHERE table_schema = 'pos'
          AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE'
    ) LOOP
        -- Check if table has updated_at column
        IF EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM information_schema.columns
            WHERE table_schema = 'pos'
              AND table_name = v_table_name
              AND column_name = 'updated_at'
        ) THEN
            EXECUTE format('
                DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_update_updated_at_%I ON pos.%I;
                CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_updated_at_%I
                    BEFORE UPDATE ON pos.%I
                    FOR EACH ROW
                    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at();
            ', v_table_name, v_table_name, v_table_name, v_table_name);
        END IF;
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: DB145 - trg_application_status_tracking
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: DB145 - trg_application_status_tracking
-- Description: Trigger to track application status changes and update related fields
-- Business Case: The `trg_application_status_tracking` trigger automatically updates related fields when an application status changes. When an application moves to "Submitted," it sets the `submitted_date`. When it moves to "Clear to Close," it sets the `clear_to_close_date`. When it moves to "Closed," it sets the `closed_date`. This trigger ensures that these critical milestone timestamps are always accurate and consistent with the application status. It also handles status transitions that are not allowed, preventing invalid state changes. By automating these updates, the trigger ensures data integrity and provides accurate pipeline analytics.
-- Business Case: The business case for the `trg_application_status_tracking` trigger is ensuring accurate pipeline analytics and operational reporting. In mortgage origination, tracking milestone dates is critical for measuring cycle times, identifying bottlenecks, and demonstrating regulatory compliance. Manual tracking of these dates is error-prone and often inconsistent. By automating the milestone date updates based on status changes, Hyperion ensures that all pipeline metrics are accurate and reliable, enabling data-driven decision-making. This automation also eliminates a common source of data quality issues, reducing the need for data cleanup and manual intervention.
-- KPIs: Milestone date accuracy, Pipeline reporting reliability, Cycle time measurement accuracy, Data quality incidents, Operational reporting automation rate
-- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_application_status_tracking()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Store previous status
    NEW.previous_status := OLD.status;

    -- Update milestone dates based on status
    IF NEW.status = 'SUBMITTED' AND OLD.status = 'DRAFT' THEN
        NEW.submitted_date := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    END IF;

    IF NEW.status = 'CLEAR_TO_CLOSE' AND OLD.status NOT IN ('CLEAR_TO_CLOSE', 'CLOSED') THEN
        NEW.clear_to_close_date := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    END IF;

    IF NEW.status = 'CLOSED' AND OLD.status NOT IN ('CLOSED') THEN
        NEW.closed_date := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    END IF;

    -- Update last activity date
    NEW.last_activity_date := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

    -- Validate status transitions (prevent invalid moves)
    IF OLD.status = 'CLOSED' AND NEW.status != 'CLOSED' THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot change status from CLOSED to %', NEW.status;
    END IF;

    IF OLD.status = 'WITHDRAWN' AND NEW.status NOT IN ('CLOSED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot change status from WITHDRAWN to %', NEW.status;
    END IF;

    RETURN NEW;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error in application status tracking trigger: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_application_status_tracking IS 'Trigger to track application status changes and update related milestone dates';

-- Create trigger on application table
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_application_status_tracking ON pos.application;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_application_status_tracking
    BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON pos.application
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_application_status_tracking();

-- ====================================================================================
-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY (RLS) POLICIES
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RLS Policies for POS tables
-- Description: Row Level Security policies to enforce data isolation and access control
-- Business Case: RLS policies ensure that users can only access data they are authorized to see. This is critical for a multi-tenant platform where different lenders and users need to be isolated from each other's data. The policies enforce the principle of least privilege, ensuring that Loan Officers can only see their own applications, borrowers can only see their own data, and administrators have appropriate access. This security architecture is essential for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 compliance and builds trust with enterprise customers.
-- Feature Reference: F-09, F-71, F-84
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Enable RLS on core tables
ALTER TABLE pos.application ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.borrower ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.application_borrower ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.document_upload ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.econsent_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.field_change_history ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Create policy for application table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS application_isolation_policy ON pos.application;
CREATE POLICY application_isolation_policy ON pos.application
    USING (
        -- System admin can see everything
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        -- Loan Officer can see their own applications
        created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        -- Borrower can see applications they are associated with
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_borrower ab
            WHERE ab.application_id = application.application_id
            AND ab.borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
    );

-- Create policy for borrower table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS borrower_isolation_policy ON pos.borrower;
CREATE POLICY borrower_isolation_policy ON pos.borrower
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_borrower ab
            WHERE ab.borrower_id = borrower.borrower_id
            AND EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
                WHERE a.application_id = ab.application_id
                AND a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
            )
        )
    );

-- Create policy for document_upload table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS document_upload_isolation_policy ON pos.document_upload;
CREATE POLICY document_upload_isolation_policy ON pos.document_upload
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = document_upload.application_id
            AND a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
    );

-- Create policy for econsent_log table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS econsent_log_isolation_policy ON pos.econsent_log;
CREATE POLICY econsent_log_isolation_policy ON pos.econsent_log
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = econsent_log.application_id
            AND a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
    );

-- Create policy for field_change_history table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS field_change_history_isolation_policy ON pos.field_change_history;
CREATE POLICY field_change_history_isolation_policy ON pos.field_change_history
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        changed_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = field_change_history.application_id
            AND a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
    );

COMMENT ON TABLE pos.application IS 'Core application table with RLS policy for tenant isolation';
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.borrower IS 'Borrower table with RLS policy for tenant isolation';
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.document_upload IS 'Document upload table with RLS policy for tenant isolation';
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.econsent_log IS 'eConsent log table with RLS policy for tenant isolation';
COMMENT ON TABLE pos.field_change_history IS 'Field change history table with RLS policy for tenant isolation';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: fn_refresh_materialized_views
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: fn_refresh_materialized_views
-- Description: Refreshes all materialized views in the POS schema
-- Business Case: Materialized views need to be refreshed periodically to keep data current. This function provides a convenient way to refresh all materialized views in the correct order, respecting dependencies. It can be called from a scheduled job (e.g., every 15 minutes) or triggered by application events. By centralizing the refresh logic, it ensures that all views are refreshed consistently and efficiently.
-- KPIs: View refresh latency, Data freshness accuracy, System resource usage, Refresh success rate, View refresh automation
-- Feature Reference: F-22, F-60, F-114
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_refresh_materialized_views()
RETURNS TABLE(
    view_name TEXT,
    refresh_status VARCHAR(20),
    rows_affected INTEGER,
    refresh_duration_ms INTEGER,
    error_message TEXT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_start_time TIMESTAMP;
    v_end_time TIMESTAMP;
    v_rows_affected INTEGER;
    v_view_record RECORD;
BEGIN
    -- Refresh each materialized view in dependency order
    FOR v_view_record IN (
        SELECT viewname FROM pg_matviews
        WHERE schemaname = 'pos'
        ORDER BY viewname
    ) LOOP
        v_start_time := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

        BEGIN
            -- Refresh the view
            EXECUTE format('REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY pos.%I', v_view_record.viewname);

            -- Get row count
            EXECUTE format('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.%I', v_view_record.viewname)
            INTO v_rows_affected;

            v_end_time := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

            -- Return success
            view_name := v_view_record.viewname;
            refresh_status := 'SUCCESS';
            rows_affected := v_rows_affected;
            refresh_duration_ms := EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM (v_end_time - v_start_time));
            error_message := NULL;

            RETURN NEXT;

        EXCEPTION
            WHEN OTHERS THEN
                v_end_time := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

                -- Return failure
                view_name := v_view_record.viewname;
                refresh_status := 'FAILED';
                rows_affected := 0;
                refresh_duration_ms := EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM (v_end_time - v_start_time));
                error_message := SQLERRM;

                RETURN NEXT;

                -- Continue with next view
                CONTINUE;
        END;
    END LOOP;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error refreshing materialized views: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_refresh_materialized_views IS 'Refreshes all materialized views in the POS schema for up-to-date analytics';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: fn_get_application_summary
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: fn_get_application_summary
-- Description: Returns a comprehensive summary of an application for dashboard display
-- Business Case: This function aggregates data from multiple tables to provide a single, comprehensive view of an application's status, borrower information, financial details, and milestones. It eliminates the need for multiple separate queries, reducing application complexity and improving performance. The summary includes application status, borrower names, loan amount, DTI, LTV, AUS status, disclosure status, and task completion. This consolidated view is essential for the LO pipeline dashboard and borrower portal.
-- KPIs: Dashboard load time, Query complexity reduction, Data consistency, Application summary accuracy, Dashboard user satisfaction
-- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_get_application_summary(
    p_application_id UUID
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_summary JSONB;
    v_borrower_names TEXT[];
    v_task_count INTEGER;
    v_completed_tasks INTEGER;
    v_aus_status TEXT;
    v_dti_record RECORD;
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_application_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Application ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get borrower names
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name)
    INTO v_borrower_names
    FROM pos.application_borrower ab
    JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
    WHERE ab.application_id = p_application_id
      AND ab.role_type = 'PRIMARY_BORROWER';

    -- Get task counts
    SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed THEN 1 END)
    INTO v_task_count, v_completed_tasks
    FROM pos.task
    WHERE application_id = p_application_id
      AND status != 'CANCELLED';

    -- Get AUS status
    SELECT a.finding_type::TEXT INTO v_aus_status
    FROM pos.aus_submission a
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id
      AND a.is_active = TRUE
    ORDER BY a.submission_timestamp DESC
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Get DTI
    SELECT * INTO v_dti_record
    FROM pos.fn_calculate_dti(p_application_id)
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Build summary JSON
    v_summary := jsonb_build_object(
        'application_id', p_application_id,
        'loan_number', (SELECT loan_number FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'status', (SELECT status::TEXT FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'borrower_names', v_borrower_names,
        'loan_amount', (SELECT loan_amount FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'interest_rate', (SELECT interest_rate FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'dti_front', v_dti_record.front_end_ratio,
        'dti_back', v_dti_record.back_end_ratio,
        'dti_status', v_dti_record.dti_status,
        'ltv', (SELECT ltv_ratio FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'aus_status', v_aus_status,
        'task_count', v_task_count,
        'completed_tasks', v_completed_tasks,
        'task_completion_percent', CASE
            WHEN v_task_count > 0 THEN ROUND((v_completed_tasks * 100.0 / v_task_count), 2)
            ELSE 100
        END,
        'submitted_date', (SELECT submitted_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'created_date', (SELECT created_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'days_since_created', EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (SELECT created_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id)))
    );

    RETURN v_summary;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error getting application summary for %: %', p_application_id, SQLERRM;
        RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', SQLERRM, 'application_id', p_application_id);
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_get_application_summary IS 'Returns a comprehensive summary of an application for dashboard display';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- TABLE: DB101 - borrower_activity_log
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Table: DB101 - borrower_activity_log
     -- Description: Clickstream data tracking exact button clicks and field focuses
     -- Business Case: The borrower_activity_log table captures granular clickstream data of every user interaction within the POS, including button clicks, field focuses, form submissions, and navigation events. This table is the foundation of the User Behavior Analytics module, enabling product managers to reconstruct the exact user journey and identify UX friction points. By linking activity logs to specific visitor sessions and application steps, the system can correlate user behavior with conversion outcomes, such as abandonment or submission. The data supports the exit intent detection and session timeout warning features, allowing the system to intervene when a user exhibits hesitation or frustration. It also feeds the AI friction detection engine, automatically flagging application steps with high abandonment rates and triggering proactive interventions. This structured clickstream data is essential for continuous UX optimization and A/B testing validation.
     -- Business Case: The business case for the borrower_activity_log table is founded on the necessity to move from guessing about user behavior to scientifically optimizing the application funnel. In traditional POS platforms, there is a complete blind spot regarding how users interact with the interface, leading to a 60% application abandonment rate that lenders simply accept as a cost of doing business. By capturing granular clickstream data, Hyperion enables product teams to identify exactly where borrowers drop off, which fields cause confusion, and which UX elements drive conversion. This data-driven approach reduces the abandonment rate, increases application completion rates, and optimizes the cost per funded loan. Strategically, the activity log feeds the AI Core, enabling the system to predict abandonment before it happens and proactively intervene with tooltips, chat prompts, or exit-intent offers.
     -- KPIs: Application abandonment rate by step, User friction score, Feature adoption rate, Field hesitation time, A/B test conversion lift
     -- Feature Reference: F-13, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.borrower_activity_log (
         -- Primary key
         borrower_activity_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

         -- Foreign keys
         visitor_session_id UUID NOT NULL,

         -- Activity details
         element_id VARCHAR(255),
         element_type VARCHAR(50) CHECK (element_type IN ('BUTTON', 'INPUT', 'SELECT', 'LINK', 'NAV', 'CHECKBOX', 'RADIO', 'TEXTAREA', 'DROPDOWN', 'MODAL')),
         action_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (action_type IN ('CLICK', 'FOCUS', 'BLUR', 'CHANGE', 'SUBMIT', 'LOAD', 'EXIT_INTENT', 'SCROLL', 'HOVER', 'DRAG_DROP', 'KEY_PRESS')),
         page_url VARCHAR(500),
         page_title VARCHAR(255),
         application_step VARCHAR(100),
         section_name VARCHAR(100),

         -- Field context (if applicable)
         field_name VARCHAR(255),
         field_label VARCHAR(255),
         field_old_value TEXT,
         field_new_value TEXT,
         field_validation_status VARCHAR(20) CHECK (field_validation_status IN ('VALID', 'INVALID', 'PENDING', 'SKIPPED')),

         -- Timing
         event_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
         time_spent_on_page_seconds INTEGER CHECK (time_spent_on_page_seconds >= 0),
         time_since_last_event_seconds INTEGER CHECK (time_since_last_event_seconds >= 0),

         -- User context
         user_id UUID,
         user_role VARCHAR(50) CHECK (user_role IN ('BORROWER', 'LOAN_OFFICER', 'PROCESSOR', 'UNDERWRITER', 'SYSTEM')),

         -- Device context
         screen_size VARCHAR(20),
         viewport_size VARCHAR(20),
         device_orientation VARCHAR(10) CHECK (device_orientation IN ('PORTRAIT', 'LANDSCAPE', 'UNKNOWN')),

         -- Browser context
         browser_language VARCHAR(10),
         referrer_url VARCHAR(500),

         -- Performance metrics
         page_load_time_ms INTEGER,
         api_response_time_ms INTEGER,
         network_quality VARCHAR(20) CHECK (network_quality IN ('FAST', 'MEDIUM', 'SLOW', 'UNKNOWN')),

         -- Metadata
         metadata JSONB,
         tags TEXT[],

         -- Audit trail
         created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Constraints
         CONSTRAINT fk_borrower_activity_log_session FOREIGN KEY (visitor_session_id)
             REFERENCES pos.visitor_session(visitor_session_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
     );
     COMMENT ON TABLE pos.borrower_activity_log IS 'Clickstream data tracking exact button clicks and field focuses, enabling UX optimization and friction detection';

     -- TABLE: DB103 - rate_lock_history
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Table: DB103 - rate_lock_history
     -- Description: Tracks complete history of rate locks and lock extensions
     -- Business Case: The rate_lock_history table provides a comprehensive audit trail of all rate lock activities, including initial locks, extensions, re-locks, and expirations. It captures the lock terms, rates, market conditions, and approval workflows. This table is critical for secondary marketing operations, providing the detailed data needed to hedge pipeline risk and manage fallout. It also supports borrower transparency by allowing the system to display the complete rate lock history to the borrower. The table enables the system to automatically trigger rate lock expiration warnings and extension workflows, preventing costly lock expirations that can eat into lender margins.
     -- Business Case: The rate_lock_history table is essential for capital markets risk management and borrower trust. Rate locks are a critical commitment from the lender to the borrower, and any errors in rate lock management can result in significant financial losses or regulatory penalties. By maintaining a complete, immutable history of all rate lock activities, Hyperion ensures that there is a clear audit trail for every rate lock decision. Operationally, this table enables automated rate lock monitoring, alerting LOs and secondary marketing teams when locks are approaching expiration. Strategically, analyzing rate lock patterns provides insights into market trends, borrower behavior, and pipeline risk, enabling more accurate hedging and improved profitability.
     -- KPIs: Rate lock accuracy, Lock expiration rate, Lock extension rate, Secondary market hedge effectiveness, Borrower rate lock satisfaction
     -- Feature Reference: F-66, F-146
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.rate_lock_history (
         -- Primary key
         rate_lock_history_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

         -- Foreign keys
         application_id UUID NOT NULL,

         -- Lock details
         lock_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (lock_type IN ('INITIAL', 'EXTENSION', 'RE_LOCK', 'EXPIRATION', 'CANCELLATION')),
         lock_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
         lock_expiration_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
         lock_duration_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lock_duration_days > 0),

         -- Rate details
         locked_rate NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL CHECK (locked_rate >= 0 AND locked_rate <= 100),
         locked_apr NUMERIC(7,4),
         locked_margin NUMERIC(7,4),

         -- Pricing
         locked_points NUMERIC(7,4),
         locked_lender_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
         locked_third_party_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
         total_lock_cost NUMERIC(12,2),

         -- Market context
         market_rate_at_lock NUMERIC(7,4),
         rate_spread_at_lock NUMERIC(7,4),

         -- Approval
         requested_by UUID NOT NULL,
         approved_by UUID,
         approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
         approval_notes TEXT,

         -- Extension details (if extension)
         previous_lock_id UUID,
         extension_reason VARCHAR(255),
         extension_approved_by UUID,
         extension_approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

         -- Status
         lock_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' CHECK (lock_status IN ('ACTIVE', 'EXPIRED', 'CANCELLED', 'EXTENDED', 'RE_LOCKED', 'FUNDED')),

         -- Secondary market
         hedge_instrument VARCHAR(50),
         hedge_reference VARCHAR(100),

         -- Audit trail
         created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
         updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Metadata
         notes TEXT,

         -- Constraints
         CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_history_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
             REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
         CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_history_previous FOREIGN KEY (previous_lock_id)
             REFERENCES pos.rate_lock_history(rate_lock_history_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
         CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_history_requested_by FOREIGN KEY (requested_by)
             REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
         CONSTRAINT rate_lock_history_dates_check CHECK (lock_expiration_date > lock_date)
     );
     COMMENT ON TABLE pos.rate_lock_history IS 'Tracks complete history of rate locks and lock extensions, enabling secondary market risk management';

     -- Table: DB106 - document_version
     -- Description: Tracks version history of uploaded documents
     -- Business Case: The document_version table tracks the version history of documents uploaded by borrowers, enabling document version control and rollback capabilities.          storage_file_path VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
         file_size_bytes BIGINT CHECK (file_size_bytes >= 0),
         file_hash VARCHAR(64),

         -- Version metadata
         version_reason VARCHAR(255),
         superseded_by_version_id UUID,

         -- Version status
         is_current BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
         is_archived BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,

         -- Audit trail
         created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
         updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Metadata
         notes TEXT,

         -- Constraints
         CONSTRAINT fk_document_version_document FOREIGN KEY (document_upload_id)
             REFERENCES pos.document_upload(document_upload_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
         CONSTRAINT fk_document_version_superseded FOREIGN KEY (superseded_by_version_id)
             REFERENCES pos.document_version(document_version_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
         CONSTRAINT document_version_unique UNIQUE (document_upload_id, version_number)
     );
     COMMENT ON TABLE pos.document_version IS 'Tracks version history of uploaded documents, enabling version control and audit compliance';

     -- Indexes for document_version table
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_version_document ON pos.document_version (document_upload_id);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_version_version_number ON pos.document_version (version_number);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_version_is_current ON pos.document_version (is_current);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_version_is_archived ON pos.document_version (is_archived);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_version_version_timestamp ON pos.document_version (version_timestamp);

     -- Business Case: The borrower_validation_cache table stores pre-computed validation results for borrower data fields, enabling rapid validation checks without re-querying the underlying data. It caches validation results such as address verification, employment verification, and credit score validation. This table significantly improves application performance by reducing the need for repeated validations, especially for frequently accessed fields.      -- Business Case: The borrower_validation_cache table is critical for delivering a responsive, real-time user experience. By caching validation results, Hyperion provides sub-second feedback on data quality and eligibility. Operationally, this reduces the load on external validation APIs and improves system performance. Strategically, the cached validation data enables the system to proactively identify and correct data quality issues before they cause downstream problems, reducing rework and improving cycle times.
     -- KPIs: Validation cache hit rate, Validation response time, API call reduction, System performance improvement, Data quality improvement
     -- Feature Reference: F-13, F-81, F-82
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.borrower_validation_cache (
         -- Primary key
         borrower_validation_cache_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

         validation_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (validation_type IN ('ADDRESS', 'EMPLOYMENT', 'CREDIT_SCORE', 'INCOME', 'ASSET', 'OFAC', 'GEOCODING')),
         validation_key VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

         -- Validation result
         validation_result JSONB NOT NULL,
         validation_score NUMERIC(5,2) CHECK (validation_score >= 0 AND validation_score <= 100),

         -- Status

         -- Timestamps
         validated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
         expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

         -- Context
         source VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('API', 'CACHE', 'SYSTEM', 'MANUAL')),

         -- Audit trail

         updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Metadata
         notes TEXT,

         -- Constraints
         CONSTRAINT fk_borrower_validation_cache_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
             REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
         CONSTRAINT borrower_validation_cache_unique UNIQUE (borrower_id, validation_type, validation_key)
     );
     COMMENT ON TABLE pos.borrower_validation_cache IS 'Caches validation results for borrower data to improve performance and reduce API calls';

     -- TABLE: DB109 - application_workflow_state

     -- Table: DB109 - application_workflow_state
     -- Description: Tracks the current workflow state and progress of an application
     -- Business Case: The application_workflow_state table tracks the current state of the application through the various stages of the mortgage origination workflow, from initial application through funding. It stores the current step, the timestamp of when the step was reached, and any related metadata. This table enables the system to implement complex workflow orchestration, ensuring that applications progress through the correct steps and that all required actions are completed. It also supports the borrower portal status display, showing borrowers exactly where they are in the process.
     -- Business Case: The application_workflow_state table is essential for workflow orchestration and borrower transparency. In complex mortgage origination processes, it's critical to know exactly where each application is in the workflow and what actions are required next. This table enables the system to automatically route applications to the right teams, trigger notifications, and ensure that no steps are missed. Operationally, it provides complete visibility into pipeline status and workflow bottlenecks. Strategically, workflow state data enables predictive analytics, allowing the system to identify which applications are at risk of delay and proactively intervene.
     -- KPIs: Workflow completion rate, Average time per workflow step, Bottleneck identification, Workflow automation rate, Application routing accuracy
     -- Feature Reference: F-22, F-52, F-117

         -- Step tracking

         available_actions TEXT[],

             REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
