     -- ====================================================================================
     -- VIEW: DB110 - vw_application_pipeline
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- View: DB110 - vw_application_pipeline
     -- Description: Comprehensive view of the application pipeline for dashboard reporting
     -- Business Case: The application_pipeline view provides a comprehensive, real-time view of all applications in the pipeline, including application details, borrower information, status, AUS results, and key metrics. This view is the foundation for the LO dashboard, pipeline management, and executive reporting. It aggregates data from multiple tables into a single, easy-to-query view, eliminating complex joins and improving dashboard performance. By providing a single source of truth for pipeline data, it ensures consistency across all reporting and analytics.
     -- Business Case: The application_pipeline view is critical for pipeline management and operational visibility. LOs, processors, and executives need to quickly understand the status of all applications in the pipeline, including key metrics like volume, velocity, and bottlenecks. This view provides that visibility in a single, well-structured format. Operationally, it enables rapid identification of at-risk applications and bottlenecks. Strategically, it provides the data needed for pipeline forecasting and resource planning, enabling proactive management of loan volume and capacity.
     -- KPIs: Pipeline visibility, Dashboard load time, Data consistency, Operational decision speed, Forecast accuracy
     -- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_application_pipeline AS
     SELECT
         a.application_id,
         a.loan_number,
         a.loan_purpose,
         a.loan_amount,
         a.interest_rate,
         a.status,
         a.created_date,
         a.submitted_date,
         a.clear_to_close_date,
         a.closed_date,
         a.created_by AS lo_user_id,
         a.referral_source,
         a.lead_source,

         -- Borrower information
         (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name)
          FROM pos.application_borrower ab
          JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
          WHERE ab.application_id = a.application_id
            AND ab.role_type = 'PRIMARY_BORROWER') AS borrower_names,

         -- Key metrics
         dti.front_end_ratio,
         dti.back_end_ratio,
         dti.dti_status,
         a.ltv_ratio,

         -- AUS status
         (SELECT finding_type::TEXT
          FROM pos.aus_submission aus
          WHERE aus.application_id = a.application_id
            AND aus.is_active = TRUE
          ORDER BY aus.submission_timestamp DESC
          LIMIT 1) AS aus_status,

         -- Task completion
         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND status != 'CANCELLED') AS total_tasks,
         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND is_completed = TRUE) AS completed_tasks,

         -- Document status
         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.document_upload WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND is_active = TRUE) AS total_documents,
         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.document_upload WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND ocr_status = 'CLASSIFIED') AS classified_documents,

         -- Days in pipeline
         EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) AS days_in_pipeline,

         -- Age category
         CASE
             WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 7 THEN '0-7 Days'
             WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 15 THEN '8-15 Days'
             WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 30 THEN '16-30 Days'
             ELSE '30+ Days'
         END AS age_category,

         -- Created date parts for grouping
         DATE_TRUNC('day', a.created_date) AS created_day,
         DATE_TRUNC('week', a.created_date) AS created_week,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', a.created_date) AS created_month,
         EXTRACT(YEAR FROM a.created_date) AS created_year,
         EXTRACT(MONTH FROM a.created_date) AS created_month_num

     FROM pos.application a
     LEFT JOIN pos.fn_calculate_dti(a.application_id) dti ON TRUE
     WHERE a.status NOT IN ('DRAFT')
       AND a.status NOT IN ('CLOSED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED')
     ORDER BY a.created_date DESC;

     COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_application_pipeline IS 'Comprehensive view of the application pipeline for dashboard reporting and pipeline management';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- VIEW: DB111 - vw_borrower_portal_dashboard
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- View: DB111 - vw_borrower_portal_dashboard
     -- Description: View for borrower portal dashboard showing application status and tasks
     -- Business Case: The borrower_portal_dashboard view provides a comprehensive, borrower-friendly view of their application status, tasks, and milestones. It aggregates data from multiple tables into a single view optimized for the borrower portal experience. The view includes the application status, upcoming tasks, recent activity, and key milestones. By providing a single source of truth for the borrower portal, it ensures consistency and reduces the complexity of building the portal interface.
     -- Business Case: The borrower_portal_dashboard view is essential for delivering a consumer-grade borrower experience. Borrowers want a single, unified view of their loan application status and what they need to do next. This view provides that unified view, simplifying the development of the borrower portal and ensuring a consistent experience. Operationally, it reduces the complexity of portal development and maintenance. Strategically, it enables the platform to deliver a best-in-class borrower experience that drives satisfaction and repeat business.
     -- KPIs: Portal load time, Borrower engagement rate, Task completion rate, Portal satisfaction score, Portal feature adoption
     -- Feature Reference: F-51, F-52, F-65, F-118
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_borrower_portal_dashboard AS
     SELECT
         a.application_id,
         a.loan_number,
         a.status,
         a.loan_amount,
         a.interest_rate,
         a.ltv_ratio,
         a.created_date,
         a.submitted_date,
         a.clear_to_close_date,

         -- Borrower info
         b.borrower_id,
         b.first_name,
         b.last_name,
         b.email,

         -- Tasks
         t.task_count AS total_tasks,
         t.completed_count AS completed_tasks,
         t.overdue_count AS overdue_tasks,
         CASE
             WHEN t.task_count > 0 THEN ROUND((t.completed_count * 100.0 / t.task_count), 2)
             ELSE 100
         END AS task_completion_percent,

         -- Documents
         d.total_documents,
         d.uploaded_documents,

         -- Recent activity
         (SELECT jsonb_agg(row_to_json(activity))
          FROM (
              SELECT action_type, event_timestamp
              FROM pos.borrower_activity_log
              WHERE borrower_id = b.borrower_id
              ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
              LIMIT 5
          ) activity) AS recent_activity,

         -- Next steps
         (SELECT row_to_json(next_step)
          FROM (
              SELECT task_name, due_date, task_priority
              FROM pos.task
              WHERE application_id = a.application_id
                AND is_completed = FALSE
                AND status != 'CANCELLED'
              ORDER BY task_priority ASC, due_date ASC
              LIMIT 1
          ) next_step) AS next_step,

         -- AUS status
         (SELECT finding_type::TEXT || ' - ' || finding_description
          FROM pos.aus_submission
          WHERE application_id = a.application_id
            AND is_active = TRUE
          ORDER BY submission_timestamp DESC
          LIMIT 1) AS aus_status,

         -- Rate lock status
         (SELECT lock_status FROM pos.rate_lock_history
          WHERE application_id = a.application_id
          ORDER BY lock_date DESC
          LIMIT 1) AS rate_lock_status

     FROM pos.application a
     JOIN pos.application_borrower ab ON ab.application_id = a.application_id
     JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
     LEFT JOIN (
         SELECT
             application_id,
             COUNT(*) AS task_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed THEN 1 END) AS completed_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed = FALSE AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE THEN 1 END) AS overdue_count
         FROM pos.task
         WHERE status != 'CANCELLED'
         GROUP BY application_id
     ) t ON t.application_id = a.application_id
     LEFT JOIN (
         SELECT
             application_id,
             COUNT(*) AS total_documents,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN ocr_status != 'UPLOADED' THEN 1 END) AS uploaded_documents
         FROM pos.document_upload
         WHERE is_active = TRUE
         GROUP BY application_id
     ) d ON d.application_id = a.application_id
     WHERE ab.role_type IN ('PRIMARY_BORROWER', 'CO_BORROWER');

     COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_borrower_portal_dashboard IS 'View for borrower portal dashboard showing application status and tasks';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB112 - fn_update_application_status
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB112 - fn_update_application_status
     -- Description: Safely updates application status with validation and audit logging
     -- Business Case: The fn_update_application_status function provides a controlled interface for updating application status, enforcing valid status transitions, and ensuring proper audit logging. It validates that the requested status transition is allowed, updates the application status and related fields, and logs the change. This function centralizes status management logic, preventing invalid status changes and ensuring consistent behavior across the system.
     -- Business Case: The fn_update_application_status function is critical for maintaining data integrity and ensuring proper workflow management. Allowing arbitrary status changes from any part of the application can lead to data corruption and workflow errors. By centralizing status update logic in a controlled function, Hyperion ensures that status changes are always valid, audited, and handled consistently. Operationally, this reduces bugs and simplifies development. Strategically, it ensures the integrity of pipeline data and enables accurate reporting and analytics.
     -- KPIs: Status update validation rate, Invalid status transition prevention, Audit completeness, Status change latency, Developer productivity improvement
     -- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_update_application_status(
         p_application_id UUID,
         p_new_status VARCHAR(50),
         p_status_reason TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
         p_notes TEXT DEFAULT NULL
     )
     RETURNS TABLE(
         success BOOLEAN,
         message TEXT,
         old_status VARCHAR(50),
         new_status VARCHAR(50)
     )
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     DECLARE
         v_current_status VARCHAR(50);
         v_old_status VARCHAR(50);
         v_success BOOLEAN := FALSE;
         v_message TEXT := '';
         v_valid_transition BOOLEAN := FALSE;

         -- Valid status transitions
         v_valid_transitions JSONB := jsonb_build_object(
             'DRAFT', ARRAY['SUBMITTED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'EXPIRED'],
             'SUBMITTED', ARRAY['IN_PROGRESS', 'AUS_PENDING', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'IN_PROGRESS', ARRAY['AUS_PENDING', 'CONDITIONAL_APPROVAL', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'AUS_PENDING', ARRAY['AUS_APPROVED', 'AUS_REFERRED', 'AUS_DENIED', 'WITHDRAWN'],
             'AUS_APPROVED', ARRAY['CONDITIONAL_APPROVAL', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'AUS_REFERRED', ARRAY['IN_PROGRESS', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'AUS_DENIED', ARRAY['SUBMITTED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'CONDITIONAL_APPROVAL', ARRAY['CLEAR_TO_CLOSE', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'CLEAR_TO_CLOSE', ARRAY['CLOSED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED'],
             'CLOSED', ARRAY[],
             'WITHDRAWN', ARRAY[],
             'DECLINED', ARRAY[],
             'EXPIRED', ARRAY[]
         );
     BEGIN
         -- Get current status
         SELECT status INTO v_current_status
         FROM pos.application
         WHERE application_id = p_application_id
         FOR UPDATE;

         IF NOT FOUND THEN
             v_message := 'Application not found';
             RETURN QUERY SELECT FALSE, v_message, NULL::VARCHAR, NULL::VARCHAR;
             RETURN;
         END IF;

         -- Check if status change is valid
         IF v_current_status = p_new_status THEN
             v_success := TRUE;
             v_message := 'No change needed - status already ' || p_new_status;
             v_old_status := v_current_status;
             v_new_status := p_new_status;

             RETURN QUERY SELECT v_success, v_message, v_old_status, v_new_status;
             RETURN;
         END IF;

         -- Validate transition
         IF (v_valid_transitions->v_current_status) IS NOT NULL THEN
             IF p_new_status = ANY (ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(v_valid_transitions->v_current_status))) THEN
                 v_valid_transition := TRUE;
             END IF;
         END IF;

         IF NOT v_valid_transition THEN
             v_message := 'Invalid status transition from ' || v_current_status || ' to ' || p_new_status;
             RETURN QUERY SELECT FALSE, v_message, v_current_status, p_new_status;
             RETURN;
         END IF;

         -- Update application status
         UPDATE pos.application
         SET status = p_new_status::pos.typ_application_status_enum,
             status_reason = COALESCE(p_status_reason, status_reason),
             notes = CASE
                 WHEN p_notes IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(notes, '') || E'\n' || p_notes
                 ELSE notes
             END,
             updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
             updated_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
         WHERE application_id = p_application_id;

         -- Log the change
         PERFORM pos.fn_log_application_event(p_application_id, 'STATUS_CHANGE', jsonb_build_object(
             'old_status', v_current_status,
             'new_status', p_new_status,
             'reason', p_status_reason,
             'user_id', current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
         ));

         v_success := TRUE;
         v_message := 'Status updated successfully';
         v_old_status := v_current_status;
         v_new_status := p_new_status;

         RETURN QUERY SELECT v_success, v_message, v_old_status, v_new_status;

     EXCEPTION
         WHEN OTHERS THEN
             v_message := 'Error updating status: ' || SQLERRM;
             RETURN QUERY SELECT FALSE, v_message, v_current_status, p_new_status;
             RETURN;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_update_application_status IS 'Safely updates application status with validation and audit logging';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB113 - fn_log_application_event
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB113 - fn_log_application_event
     -- Description: Logs application events for audit and analytics
     -- Business Case: The fn_log_application_event function provides a standardized interface for logging application lifecycle events, such as status changes, document uploads, disclosure deliveries, and borrower actions. It captures the event type, the related data, and the timestamp. This function centralizes event logging logic, ensuring consistent and complete event capture across the system. The event log provides the foundation for application timeline tracking, audit trails, and behavioral analytics.
     -- Business Case: The fn_log_application_event function is critical for application lifecycle tracking and analytics. Understanding what happened, when, and why is essential for both operational management and regulatory compliance. This function provides a standardized way to capture all application events. Operationally, it enables the system to display a complete timeline of the application for borrowers and LOs. Strategically, the aggregated event data provides insights into application behavior, bottlenecks, and process efficiency, enabling continuous optimization.
     -- KPIs: Event logging completeness, Timeline accuracy, Audit trail completeness, Analytics data quality, System performance impact
     -- Feature Reference: F-22, F-117, F-134
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.application_event_log (
         -- Primary key
         application_event_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

         -- Foreign keys
         application_id UUID NOT NULL,
         user_id UUID,

         -- Event details
         event_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (event_type IN ('STATUS_CHANGE', 'DOCUMENT_UPLOAD', 'DISCLOSURE_DELIVERY', 'DISCLOSURE_SIGN', 'AUS_SUBMISSION', 'AUS_RESULT', 'TASK_COMPLETED', 'BORROWER_ACTION', 'LO_ACTION', 'SYSTEM_ACTION')),
         event_subtype VARCHAR(50),
         event_data JSONB,

         -- Timestamps
         event_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Context
         ip_address INET,
         user_agent TEXT,
         session_id VARCHAR(100),

         -- Audit trail
         created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

         -- Constraints
         CONSTRAINT fk_application_event_log_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
             REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
     );
     COMMENT ON TABLE pos.application_event_log IS 'Logs application events for audit and analytics';

     -- Indexes for application_event_log table
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_application ON pos.application_event_log (application_id);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_event_type ON pos.application_event_log (event_type);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_event_timestamp ON pos.application_event_log (event_timestamp);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_user_id ON pos.application_event_log (user_id);
     CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_session_id ON pos.application_event_log (session_id);

     -- Log function
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_log_application_event(
         p_application_id UUID,
         p_event_type VARCHAR(50),
         p_event_data JSONB DEFAULT NULL,
         p_ip_address INET DEFAULT NULL,
         p_user_agent TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
         p_session_id VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT NULL
     )
     RETURNS UUID
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     DECLARE
         v_event_log_id UUID;
         v_user_id UUID;
     BEGIN
         -- Get current user
         v_user_id := current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID;

         -- Insert event log entry
         INSERT INTO pos.application_event_log (
             application_id,
             user_id,
             event_type,
             event_data,
             event_timestamp,
             ip_address,
             user_agent,
             session_id,
             created_at
         ) VALUES (
             p_application_id,
             v_user_id,
             p_event_type,
             p_event_data,
             CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
             COALESCE(p_ip_address, inet_client_addr()),
             COALESCE(p_user_agent, current_setting('app.user_agent', TRUE)),
             COALESCE(p_session_id, current_setting('app.session_id', TRUE)),
             CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
         ) RETURNING application_event_log_id INTO v_event_log_id;

         RETURN v_event_log_id;

     EXCEPTION
         WHEN OTHERS THEN
             RAISE WARNING 'Error logging application event: %', SQLERRM;
             RETURN NULL;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_log_application_event IS 'Logs application events for audit and analytics';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB114 - fn_get_applications_by_lender
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB114 - fn_get_applications_by_lender
     -- Description: Retrieves all applications for a specific lender with filtering options
     -- Business Case: The fn_get_applications_by_lender function provides a comprehensive, filtered view of applications for a specific lender. It supports filtering by status, date range, loan purpose, and other key criteria. This function is used by the lender admin portal to manage their loan pipeline. It provides the data needed for pipeline management, reporting, and operational oversight.
     -- Business Case: The fn_get_applications_by_lender function is essential for lender portfolio management. Lenders need to quickly access and manage their loan pipeline, including filtering, sorting, and reporting on applications. This function provides that capability in a performant and secure manner. Operationally, it enables LOs and managers to efficiently manage their portfolio. Strategically, it provides the data needed for portfolio analytics and forecasting.
     -- KPIs: Query performance, Filter accuracy, Data completeness, User satisfaction, Operational efficiency
     -- Feature Reference: F-22, F-51, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_get_applications_by_lender(
         p_lender_id UUID,
         p_status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
         p_date_from DATE DEFAULT NULL,
         p_date_to DATE DEFAULT NULL,
         p_loan_purpose VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
         p_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 100,
         p_offset INTEGER DEFAULT 0
     )
     RETURNS TABLE(
         application_id UUID,
         loan_number VARCHAR(20),
         status VARCHAR(50),
         loan_amount NUMERIC(18,2),
         loan_purpose VARCHAR(50),
         borrower_name TEXT,
         created_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
         submitted_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
         days_in_pipeline INTEGER,
         has_task BOOLEAN,
         task_count INTEGER,
         task_completion_rate NUMERIC(5,2)
     )
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     BEGIN
         RETURN QUERY
         SELECT
             a.application_id,
             a.loan_number,
             a.status::TEXT,
             a.loan_amount,
             a.loan_purpose::TEXT,
             (SELECT string_agg(b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name, ', ')
              FROM pos.application_borrower ab
              JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
              WHERE ab.application_id = a.application_id
                AND ab.role_type = 'PRIMARY_BORROWER') AS borrower_name,
             a.created_date,
             a.submitted_date,
             EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date))::INTEGER AS days_in_pipeline,
             EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND is_completed = FALSE) AS has_task,
             (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND status != 'CANCELLED') AS task_count,
             (SELECT ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)), 2)
              FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND status != 'CANCELLED') AS task_completion_rate
         FROM pos.application a
         WHERE a.created_by = p_lender_id
           AND (p_status IS NULL OR a.status::TEXT = p_status)
           AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR a.created_date >= p_date_from)
           AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR a.created_date <= p_date_to)
           AND (p_loan_purpose IS NULL OR a.loan_purpose::TEXT = p_loan_purpose)
         ORDER BY a.created_date DESC
         LIMIT p_limit
         OFFSET p_offset;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_get_applications_by_lender IS 'Retrieves all applications for a specific lender with filtering options';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB115 - fn_validate_borrower_data
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB115 - fn_validate_borrower_data
     -- Description: Comprehensive validation of borrower data against rules and constraints
     -- Business Case: The fn_validate_borrower_data function performs comprehensive validation of borrower data, checking against business rules, regulatory requirements, and data quality standards. It validates fields such as SSN, address, income, and assets. This function is called during application submission and data updates to ensure data quality before proceeding with underwriting. By centralizing validation logic, it ensures consistent data quality across the entire system.
     -- Business Case: The fn_validate_borrower_data function is critical for data quality and regulatory compliance. Data quality issues are one of the leading causes of mortgage processing delays and rework. By validating data at the point of entry, Hyperion ensures that only high-quality data enters the pipeline. Operationally, this reduces rework and accelerates the underwriting process. Strategically, it ensures compliance with data quality requirements and reduces the risk of regulatory penalties.
     -- KPIs: Data validation pass rate, Data quality score, Validation time, Rework reduction, Compliance rate
     -- Feature Reference: F-13, F-71, F-82
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_validate_borrower_data(
         p_borrower_id UUID
     )
     RETURNS TABLE(
         validation_status VARCHAR(20),
         validation_message TEXT,
         error_fields JSONB
     )
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     DECLARE
         v_borrower_record pos.borrower%ROWTYPE;
         v_error_count INTEGER := 0;
         v_error_fields JSONB := '{}'::JSONB;
         v_error_messages TEXT[];
     BEGIN
         -- Get borrower record
         SELECT * INTO v_borrower_record
         FROM pos.borrower
         WHERE borrower_id = p_borrower_id;

         IF NOT FOUND THEN
             RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ERROR'::VARCHAR, 'Borrower not found'::TEXT, '{}'::JSONB;
             RETURN;
         END IF;

         -- Validate required fields
         IF v_borrower_record.first_name IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.first_name = '' THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{first_name}', '"Required field"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         END IF;

         IF v_borrower_record.last_name IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.last_name = '' THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{last_name}', '"Required field"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         END IF;

         IF v_borrower_record.email IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.email = '' THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{email}', '"Required field"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         ELSE
             -- Validate email format
             IF v_borrower_record.email !~ '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$' THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{email}', '"Invalid email format"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
         END IF;

         IF v_borrower_record.phone IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.phone = '' THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{phone}', '"Required field"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         ELSE
             -- Validate phone format
             IF v_borrower_record.phone !~ '^[0-9]{10,15}$' THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{phone}', '"Invalid phone format"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
         END IF;

         IF v_borrower_record.date_of_birth IS NULL THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{date_of_birth}', '"Required field"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         ELSE
             -- Validate age
             IF EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(CURRENT_DATE, v_borrower_record.date_of_birth)) < 18 THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{date_of_birth}', '"Borrower must be at least 18 years old"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
         END IF;

         IF v_borrower_record.ssn_hash IS NULL THEN
             v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{ssn}', '"SSN is required"');
             v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
         END IF;

         -- Validate address if provided
         IF v_borrower_record.address_line1 IS NOT NULL AND v_borrower_record.address_line1 != '' THEN
             IF v_borrower_record.city IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.city = '' THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{city}', '"City is required when address is provided"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
             IF v_borrower_record.state IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.state !~ '^[A-Z]{2}$' THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{state}', '"Invalid state format"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
             IF v_borrower_record.zip IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.zip !~ '^[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?$' THEN
                 v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{zip}', '"Invalid zip code format"');
                 v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
             END IF;
         END IF;

         -- Determine validation status
         IF v_error_count = 0 THEN
             RETURN QUERY SELECT 'VALID'::VARCHAR, 'All data validated successfully'::TEXT, '{}'::JSONB;
         ELSE
             RETURN QUERY SELECT 'INVALID'::VARCHAR, 'Invalid fields found'::TEXT, v_error_fields;
         END IF;

     EXCEPTION
         WHEN OTHERS THEN
             RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ERROR'::VARCHAR, SQLERRM, '{}'::JSONB;
             RETURN;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_validate_borrower_data IS 'Comprehensive validation of borrower data against rules and constraints';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- VIEW: DB116 - vw_application_metrics
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- View: DB116 - vw_application_metrics
     -- Description: Aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards
     -- Business Case: The application_metrics view provides aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards, including application volume, conversion rates, cycle times, and quality metrics. It aggregates data across all applications, providing executives with a high-level view of pipeline health and performance. This view is the foundation for executive dashboards and strategic reporting.
     -- Business Case: The application_metrics view is critical for executive decision-making. Executives need a high-level view of pipeline health and performance to make strategic decisions. This view provides that view, enabling executives to identify trends, spot issues, and make data-driven decisions. Operationally, it provides the data needed for board reporting and investor presentations. Strategically, it enables the organization to track progress against OKRs and strategic goals.
     -- KPIs: Dashboard load time, Metric accuracy, Decision-making speed, Strategic alignment, Executive satisfaction
     -- Feature Reference: F-22, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_application_metrics AS
     WITH app_stats AS (
         SELECT
             DATE_TRUNC('day', created_date) AS day,
             DATE_TRUNC('week', created_date) AS week,
             DATE_TRUNC('month', created_date) AS month,
             COUNT(*) AS total_applications,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'SUBMITTED' THEN 1 END) AS submitted_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('AUS_APPROVED', 'CONDITIONAL_APPROVAL') THEN 1 END) AS approved_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'CLEAR_TO_CLOSE' THEN 1 END) AS clear_to_close_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'CLOSED' THEN 1 END) AS closed_count,
             COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED') THEN 1 END) AS fallout_count,
             AVG(EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CASE
                 WHEN closed_date IS NOT NULL THEN closed_date - submitted_date
                 ELSE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - submitted_date
             END))) AS avg_cycle_days,
             AVG(a.loan_amount) AS avg_loan_amount,
             SUM(a.loan_amount) AS total_loan_volume
         FROM pos.application a
         WHERE created_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
         GROUP BY ROLLUP (DATE_TRUNC('day', created_date), DATE_TRUNC('week', created_date), DATE_TRUNC('month', created_date))
     )
     SELECT
         day,
         week,
         month,
         total_applications,
         submitted_count,
         approved_count,
         clear_to_close_count,
         closed_count,
         fallout_count,
         ROUND(CAST(closed_count AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(submitted_count, 0) * 100, 2) AS conversion_rate,
         ROUND(CAST(fallout_count AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(submitted_count, 0) * 100, 2) AS fallout_rate,
         ROUND(avg_cycle_days, 1) AS avg_cycle_days,
         ROUND(avg_loan_amount, 2) AS avg_loan_amount,
         ROUND(total_loan_volume, 2) AS total_loan_volume
     FROM app_stats
     ORDER BY day DESC NULLS LAST;

     COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_application_metrics IS 'Aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB117 - fn_cleanup_expired_data
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB117 - fn_cleanup_expired_data
     -- Description: Cleanup function for expired data and orphaned records
     -- Business Case: The fn_cleanup_expired_data function is a maintenance function that cleans up expired data and orphaned records to maintain database health and performance. It handles tasks such as archiving old application data, deleting expired sessions, cleaning up orphaned audit logs, and managing data retention. This function should be scheduled to run periodically as part of database maintenance.
     -- Business Case: The fn_cleanup_expired_data function is essential for maintaining database performance and managing storage costs. Over time, databases accumulate large amounts of stale and orphaned data that can impact performance and increase storage costs. By automating cleanup, Hyperion ensures that the database remains performant and that storage costs are managed effectively. Operationally, this reduces maintenance overhead and prevents performance degradation. Strategically, it ensures that the platform remains scalable and cost-effective over its 50-year lifecycle.
     -- KPIs: Data cleanup effectiveness, Database performance improvement, Storage cost reduction, Cleanup automation rate, Maintenance overhead reduction
     -- Feature Reference: F-44, F-112
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_cleanup_expired_data(
         p_dry_run BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
         p_older_than_days INTEGER DEFAULT 90
     )
     RETURNS TABLE(
         cleanup_action VARCHAR(50),
         records_affected INTEGER,
         cleanup_message TEXT
     )
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     DECLARE
         v_records_affected INTEGER;
         v_action VARCHAR(50);
         v_message TEXT;
     BEGIN
         -- Clean up expired sessions
         v_action := 'EXPIRED_SESSIONS';
         IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
             DELETE FROM pos.visitor_session
             WHERE session_end < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL;
             GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
         ELSE
             SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
             FROM pos.visitor_session
             WHERE session_end < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL;
         END IF;
         v_message := 'Cleaned up expired sessions older than ' || p_older_than_days || ' days';
         cleanup_action := v_action;
         records_affected := v_records_affected;
         cleanup_message := v_message;
         RETURN NEXT;

         -- Clean up expired magic links
         v_action := 'EXPIRED_MAGIC_LINKS';
         IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
             DELETE FROM pos.magic_link_log
             WHERE expiry_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
               AND is_used = FALSE;
             GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
         ELSE
             SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
             FROM pos.magic_link_log
             WHERE expiry_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
               AND is_used = FALSE;
         END IF;
         v_message := 'Cleaned up expired magic links';
         cleanup_action := v_action;
         records_affected := v_records_affected;
         cleanup_message := v_message;
         RETURN NEXT;

         -- Clean up expired secure links
         v_action := 'EXPIRED_SECURE_LINKS';
         IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
             UPDATE pos.secure_link_expiry
             SET is_active = FALSE,
                 is_revoked = TRUE,
                 revocation_reason = 'Auto-expired by cleanup job'
             WHERE expires_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
               AND is_active = TRUE;
             GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
         ELSE
             SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
             FROM pos.secure_link_expiry
             WHERE expires_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
               AND is_active = TRUE;
         END IF;
         v_message := 'Expired secure links deactivated';
         cleanup_action := v_action;
         records_affected := v_records_affected;
         cleanup_message := v_message;
         RETURN NEXT;

         -- Clean up orphaned activity logs
         v_action := 'ORPHANED_ACTIVITY_LOGS';
         IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
             DELETE FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
             WHERE NOT EXISTS (
                 SELECT 1 FROM pos.visitor_session vs
                 WHERE vs.visitor_session_id = bal.visitor_session_id
             );
             GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
         ELSE
             SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
             FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
             WHERE NOT EXISTS (
                 SELECT 1 FROM pos.visitor_session vs
                 WHERE vs.visitor_session_id = bal.visitor_session_id
             );
         END IF;
         v_message := 'Cleaned up orphaned activity logs';
         cleanup_action := v_action;
         records_affected := v_records_affected;
         cleanup_message := v_message;
         RETURN NEXT;

         -- Log the cleanup operation
         IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
             PERFORM pos.fn_log_application_event(
                 NULL,
                 'SYSTEM_CLEANUP',
                 jsonb_build_object(
                     'action', 'CLEANUP_EXPIRED_DATA',
                     'older_than_days', p_older_than_days,
                     'timestamp', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                 )
             );
         END IF;

     EXCEPTION
         WHEN OTHERS THEN
             RAISE WARNING 'Error in cleanup job: %', SQLERRM;
             cleanup_action := 'ERROR';
             records_affected := 0;
             cleanup_message := SQLERRM;
             RETURN NEXT;
             RETURN;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_cleanup_expired_data IS 'Cleanup function for expired data and orphaned records';

     -- ====================================================================================
     -- FUNCTION: DB118 - fn_borrower_activity_summary
     -- ====================================================================================
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     -- Function: DB118 - fn_borrower_activity_summary
     -- Description: Generates a summary of borrower activity for analytics
     -- Business Case: The fn_borrower_activity_summary function generates a comprehensive summary of borrower activity, including session counts, page views, time spent, and interaction patterns. This function is used for user behavior analytics and UX optimization. It provides the data needed to understand borrower behavior and identify opportunities for UX improvement.
     -- Business Case: The fn_borrower_activity_summary function is essential for understanding borrower behavior and optimizing the user experience. By analyzing how borrowers interact with the application, product teams can identify friction points and opportunities for improvement. Operationally, this function provides the data needed for UX analytics and reporting. Strategically, it enables continuous optimization of the borrower experience, driving higher conversion rates and borrower satisfaction.
     -- KPIs: Activity summary generation time, Analytics accuracy, UX improvement velocity, User behavior understanding, Conversion rate improvement
     -- Feature Reference: F-13, F-72, F-117
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_borrower_activity_summary(
         p_borrower_id UUID,
         p_date_from DATE DEFAULT NULL,
         p_date_to DATE DEFAULT NULL
     )
     RETURNS TABLE(
         metric_name VARCHAR(50),
         metric_value NUMERIC,
         metric_description TEXT
     )
     LANGUAGE plpgsql
     SECURITY DEFINER
     AS $$
     DECLARE
         v_total_sessions INTEGER;
         v_total_actions INTEGER;
         v_avg_session_duration NUMERIC;
         v_completion_rate NUMERIC;
         v_abandonment_rate NUMERIC;
         v_time_per_step NUMERIC;
     BEGIN
         -- Validate input
         IF p_borrower_id IS NULL THEN
             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Borrower ID cannot be null';
         END IF;

         -- Get session metrics
         SELECT
             COUNT(DISTINCT vs.visitor_session_id),
             COUNT(bal.borrower_activity_log_id),
             AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (vs.session_end - vs.session_start)) / 60)
         INTO v_total_sessions, v_total_actions, v_avg_session_duration
         FROM pos.visitor_session vs
         LEFT JOIN pos.borrower_activity_log bal ON bal.visitor_session_id = vs.visitor_session_id
         WHERE vs.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
           AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR vs.session_start >= p_date_from)
           AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR vs.session_start <= p_date_to);

         -- Get completion rate
         SELECT
             COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN vs.session_abandoned = FALSE THEN vs.visitor_session_id END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT vs.visitor_session_id), 0)
         INTO v_completion_rate
         FROM pos.visitor_session vs
         WHERE vs.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
           AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR vs.session_start >= p_date_from)
           AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR vs.session_start <= p_date_to);

         -- Get abandonment rate
         v_abandonment_rate := 100 - COALESCE(v_completion_rate, 0);

         -- Get average time per application step
         SELECT
             AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_timestamp - current_timestamp))) / 60
         INTO v_time_per_step
         FROM (
             SELECT
                 bal.event_timestamp AS current_timestamp,
                 LEAD(bal.event_timestamp) OVER (ORDER BY bal.event_timestamp) AS next_timestamp
             FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
             WHERE bal.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
               AND bal.action_type = 'LOAD'
               AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR bal.event_timestamp >= p_date_from)
               AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR bal.event_timestamp <= p_date_to)
         ) step_times
         WHERE next_timestamp IS NOT NULL;

         -- Return results
         metric_name := 'total_sessions';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_total_sessions, 0);
         metric_description := 'Total number of sessions';
         RETURN NEXT;

         metric_name := 'total_actions';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_total_actions, 0);
         metric_description := 'Total number of user actions';
         RETURN NEXT;

         metric_name := 'avg_session_duration_minutes';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_avg_session_duration, 0);
         metric_description := 'Average session duration in minutes';
         RETURN NEXT;

         metric_name := 'session_completion_rate';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_completion_rate, 0);
         metric_description := 'Percentage of sessions that were completed';
         RETURN NEXT;

         metric_name := 'session_abandonment_rate';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_abandonment_rate, 0);
         metric_description := 'Percentage of sessions that were abandoned';
         RETURN NEXT;

         metric_name := 'avg_time_per_step_minutes';
         metric_value := COALESCE(v_time_per_step, 0);
         metric_description := 'Average time spent per application step in minutes';
         RETURN NEXT;

     EXCEPTION
         WHEN OTHERS THEN
             RAISE WARNING 'Error generating activity summary for borrower %: %', p_borrower_id, SQLERRM;
             metric_name := 'error';
             metric_value := 0;
             metric_description := SQLERRM;
             RETURN NEXT;
             RETURN;
     END;
     $$;

     COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_borrower_activity_summary IS 'Generates a summary of borrower activity for analytics';

-- Table: DB101 - borrower_activity_log
-- Description: Clickstream data tracking exact button clicks and field focuses

This table is the foundation of the User Behavior Analytics module, enabling product managers to reconstruct the exact user journey and identify UX friction points. By linking activity logs to specific visitor sessions and application steps, the system can correlate user behavior with conversion outcomes, such as abandonment or submission. The data supports the exit intent detection and session timeout warning features, allowing the system to intervene when a user exhibits hesitation or frustration. It also feeds the AI friction detection engine, automatically flagging application steps with high abandonment rates and triggering proactive interventions. This structured clickstream data is essential for continuous UX optimization and A/B testing validation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB103 - rate_lock_history
-- Description: Tracks complete history of rate locks and lock extensions
-- Business Case: The rate_lock_history table provides a comprehensive audit trail of all rate lock activities, including initial locks, extensions, re-locks, and expirations. It captures the lock terms, rates, market conditions, and approval workflows. This table is critical for secondary marketing operations, providing the detailed data needed to hedge pipeline risk and manage fallout. It also supports borrower transparency by allowing the system to display the complete rate lock history to the borrower. The table enables the system to automatically trigger rate lock expiration warnings and extension workflows, preventing costly lock expirations that can eat into lender margins.
-- KPIs: Rate lock accuracy, Lock expiration rate, Lock extension rate, Secondary market hedge effectiveness, Borrower rate lock satisfaction
-- Feature Reference: F-66, F-146
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.rate_lock_history (
    -- Primary key
    rate_lock_history_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Lock details
    lock_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (lock_type IN ('INITIAL', 'EXTENSION', 'RE_LOCK', 'EXPIRATION', 'CANCELLATION', 'AUTO_EXTENSION')),
    lock_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    lock_expiration_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    lock_duration_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lock_duration_days > 0),

    -- Rate details
    locked_rate NUMERIC(7,4) NOT NULL CHECK (locked_rate >= 0 AND locked_rate <= 100),
    locked_apr NUMERIC(7,4),
    locked_margin NUMERIC(7,4),
    locked_discount_points NUMERIC(7,4),
    locked_origination_fee NUMERIC(12,2),

    -- Pricing
    locked_lender_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
    locked_third_party_fees NUMERIC(12,2),
    total_lock_cost NUMERIC(12,2),

    -- Market context
    market_rate_at_lock NUMERIC(7,4),
    rate_spread_at_lock NUMERIC(7,4),
    lock_rate_index VARCHAR(50),

    -- Approval
    requested_by UUID NOT NULL,
    approved_by UUID,
    approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    approval_notes TEXT,
    approval_workflow JSONB,

    -- Extension details (if extension)
    previous_lock_id UUID,
    extension_reason VARCHAR(255),
    extension_approved_by UUID,
    extension_approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    extension_fee NUMERIC(12,2),

    -- Status
    lock_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' CHECK (lock_status IN ('ACTIVE', 'EXPIRED', 'CANCELLED', 'EXTENDED', 'RE_LOCKED', 'FUNDED', 'PENDING_APPROVAL')),

    -- Secondary market
    hedge_instrument VARCHAR(50),
    hedge_reference VARCHAR(100),
    hedge_executed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_history_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_rate_lock_history_previous FOREIGN KEY (previous_lock_id)
        REFERENCES pos.rate_lock_history(rate_lock_history_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    CONSTRAINT rate_lock_history_dates_check CHECK (lock_expiration_date > lock_date)
);

COMMENT ON TABLE pos.rate_lock_history IS 'Tracks complete history of rate locks and lock extensions, enabling secondary market risk management';

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB106 - document_version
-- Description: Tracks version history of uploaded documents
-- Business Case: The document_version table tracks the version history of documents uploaded by borrowers, enabling document version control and rollback capabilities. When a borrower uploads a new version of a document (e.g., an updated paystub), the system stores the new version while preserving the previous version. This table supports document comparison and audit trails, allowing underwriters to see when and why a document was replaced. It also enables the system to enforce document retention policies and automatically archive superseded versions.
-- KPIs: Document version count, Average document updates per application, Document freshness rate, Version retrieval time, Audit trail completeness
-- Feature Reference: F-15, F-77, F-112

    version_number INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (version_number >= 1),
    version_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- File details for this version
    storage_file_path VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    file_size_bytes BIGINT CHECK (file_size_bytes >= 0),
    file_hash VARCHAR(64),
    file_checksum VARCHAR(64),

    -- Version metadata
    version_reason VARCHAR(255),
    version_changes TEXT,
    superseded_by_version_id UUID,

    -- Version status

    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    created_by UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Metadata

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_document_version_document FOREIGN KEY (document_upload_id)
        REFERENCES pos.document_upload(document_upload_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_document_version_superseded FOREIGN KEY (superseded_by_version_id)
        REFERENCES pos.document_version(document_version_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    CONSTRAINT document_version_unique UNIQUE (document_upload_id, version_number)

-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table: DB108 - borrower_validation_cache
-- Description: Caches validation results for borrower data to improve performance
-- Business Case: The borrower_validation_cache table stores pre-computed validation results for borrower data fields, enabling rapid validation checks without re-querying the underlying data. It caches validation results such as address verification, employment verification, and credit score validation. This table significantly improves application performance by reducing the need for repeated validations, especially for frequently accessed fields. It supports the real-time validation engine by providing instant feedback to borrowers as they enter data.
-- KPIs: Validation cache hit rate, Validation response time, API call reduction, System performance improvement, Data quality improvement
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-81, F-82
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.borrower_validation_cache (
    -- Primary key
    borrower_validation_cache_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    borrower_id UUID NOT NULL,

    -- Validation context
    validation_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (validation_type IN ('ADDRESS', 'EMPLOYMENT', 'CREDIT_SCORE', 'INCOME', 'ASSET', 'OFAC', 'GEOCODING', 'IDENTITY', 'SOCIAL_SECURITY')),
    validation_key VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

    -- Validation result
    validation_result JSONB NOT NULL,
    validation_score NUMERIC(5,2) CHECK (validation_score >= 0 AND validation_score <= 100),

    -- Status
    validation_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING' CHECK (validation_status IN ('PENDING', 'VALID', 'INVALID', 'UNCERTAIN', 'ERROR', 'EXPIRED')),

    -- Timestamps
    validated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- Context
    source VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('API', 'CACHE', 'SYSTEM', 'MANUAL', 'EXTERNAL')),
    source_version VARCHAR(50),

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Metadata
    notes TEXT,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_borrower_validation_cache_borrower FOREIGN KEY (borrower_id)
        REFERENCES pos.borrower(borrower_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT borrower_validation_cache_unique UNIQUE (borrower_id, validation_type, validation_key)
);

COMMENT ON TABLE pos.borrower_validation_cache IS 'Caches validation results for borrower data to improve performance and reduce API calls';
