-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB110 - fn_validate_borrower_data
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB110 - fn_validate_borrower_data
-- Description: Comprehensive validation of borrower data against rules and constraints
-- Business Case: The fn_validate_borrower_data function performs comprehensive validation of borrower data, checking against business rules, regulatory requirements, and data quality standards. It validates fields such as SSN, address, income, and assets. This function is called during application submission and data updates to ensure data quality before proceeding with underwriting. By centralizing validation logic, it ensures consistent data quality across the entire system.
-- KPIs: Data validation pass rate, Data quality score, Validation time, Rework reduction, Compliance rate
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-71, F-82
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_validate_borrower_data(
    p_borrower_id UUID
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    validation_status VARCHAR(20),
    validation_message TEXT,
    error_fields JSONB,
    validation_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_borrower_record pos.borrower%ROWTYPE;
    v_error_count INTEGER := 0;
    v_error_fields JSONB := '{}'::JSONB;
    v_error_messages TEXT[];
BEGIN
    -- Get borrower record
    SELECT * INTO v_borrower_record
    FROM pos.borrower
    WHERE borrower_id = p_borrower_id;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ERROR'::VARCHAR, 'Borrower not found'::TEXT, '{}'::JSONB, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Validate required fields
    IF v_borrower_record.first_name IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.first_name = '' THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{first_name}', '"Required field"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    END IF;

    IF v_borrower_record.last_name IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.last_name = '' THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{last_name}', '"Required field"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    END IF;

    IF v_borrower_record.email IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.email = '' THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{email}', '"Required field"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    ELSE
        -- Validate email format
        IF v_borrower_record.email !~ '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$' THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{email}', '"Invalid email format"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
    END IF;

    IF v_borrower_record.phone IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.phone = '' THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{phone}', '"Required field"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    ELSE
        -- Validate phone format
        IF v_borrower_record.phone !~ '^[0-9]{10,15}$' THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{phone}', '"Invalid phone format"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
    END IF;

    IF v_borrower_record.date_of_birth IS NULL THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{date_of_birth}', '"Required field"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    ELSE
        -- Validate age
        IF EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(CURRENT_DATE, v_borrower_record.date_of_birth)) < 18 THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{date_of_birth}', '"Borrower must be at least 18 years old"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
        IF EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(CURRENT_DATE, v_borrower_record.date_of_birth)) > 120 THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{date_of_birth}', '"Invalid age"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
    END IF;

    IF v_borrower_record.ssn_hash IS NULL THEN
        v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{ssn}', '"SSN is required"');
        v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
    END IF;

    -- Validate address if provided
    IF v_borrower_record.address_line1 IS NOT NULL AND v_borrower_record.address_line1 != '' THEN
        IF v_borrower_record.city IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.city = '' THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{city}', '"City is required when address is provided"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
        IF v_borrower_record.state IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.state !~ '^[A-Z]{2}$' THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{state}', '"Invalid state format"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
        IF v_borrower_record.zip IS NULL OR v_borrower_record.zip !~ '^[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?$' THEN
            v_error_fields := jsonb_set(v_error_fields, '{zip}', '"Invalid zip code format"');
            v_error_count := v_error_count + 1;
        END IF;
    END IF;

    -- Determine validation status
    IF v_error_count = 0 THEN
        -- Cache validation result
        INSERT INTO pos.borrower_validation_cache (
            borrower_id,
            validation_type,
            validation_key,
            validation_result,
            validation_score,
            validation_status,
            validated_at,
            expires_at,
            source,
            created_at,
            updated_at
        ) VALUES (
            p_borrower_id,
            'IDENTITY',
            'COMPLETE_VALIDATION',
            jsonb_build_object('valid', true, 'fields_checked', jsonb_build_object(
                'first_name', true,
                'last_name', true,
                'email', true,
                'phone', true,
                'date_of_birth', true,
                'ssn', true,
                'address', true
            )),
            100,
            'VALID',
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '7 days',
            'SYSTEM',
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        );

        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'VALID'::VARCHAR, 'All data validated successfully'::TEXT, '{}'::JSONB, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    ELSE
        -- Cache validation failure
        INSERT INTO pos.borrower_validation_cache (
            borrower_id,
            validation_type,
            validation_key,
            validation_result,
            validation_score,
            validation_status,
            validated_at,
            expires_at,
            source,
            created_at,
            updated_at
        ) VALUES (
            p_borrower_id,
            'IDENTITY',
            'COMPLETE_VALIDATION',
            jsonb_build_object('valid', false, 'error_count', v_error_count, 'error_fields', v_error_fields),
            GREATEST(100 - (v_error_count * 10), 0),
            'INVALID',
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '1 day',
            'SYSTEM',
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        );

        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'INVALID'::VARCHAR, 'Invalid fields found'::TEXT, v_error_fields, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    END IF;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ERROR'::VARCHAR, SQLERRM, '{}'::JSONB, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
        RETURN;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_validate_borrower_data IS 'Comprehensive validation of borrower data against rules and constraints';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB111 - fn_log_application_event
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB111 - fn_log_application_event
-- Description: Logs application events for audit and analytics
-- Business Case: The fn_log_application_event function provides a standardized interface for logging application lifecycle events, such as status changes, document uploads, disclosure deliveries, and borrower actions. It captures the event type, the related data, and the timestamp. This function centralizes event logging logic, ensuring consistent and complete event capture across the system. The event log provides the foundation for application timeline tracking, audit trails, and behavioral analytics.
-- KPIs: Event logging completeness, Timeline accuracy, Audit trail completeness, Analytics data quality, System performance impact
-- Feature Reference: F-22, F-117, F-134
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pos.application_event_log (
    -- Primary key
    application_event_log_id UUID DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4() PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Foreign keys
    application_id UUID NOT NULL,
    user_id UUID,

    -- Event details
    event_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL CHECK (event_type IN ('STATUS_CHANGE', 'DOCUMENT_UPLOAD', 'DISCLOSURE_DELIVERY', 'DISCLOSURE_SIGN', 'AUS_SUBMISSION', 'AUS_RESULT', 'TASK_COMPLETED', 'BORROWER_ACTION', 'LO_ACTION', 'SYSTEM_ACTION', 'RATE_LOCK', 'APPRAISAL_ORDERED')),
    event_subtype VARCHAR(50),
    event_data JSONB,

    -- Timestamps
    event_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Context
    ip_address INET,
    user_agent TEXT,
    session_id VARCHAR(100),

    -- Audit trail
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT fk_application_event_log_application FOREIGN KEY (application_id)
        REFERENCES pos.application(application_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

COMMENT ON TABLE pos.application_event_log IS 'Logs application events for audit and analytics';

-- Indexes for application_event_log table
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_application ON pos.application_event_log (application_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_event_type ON pos.application_event_log (event_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_event_timestamp ON pos.application_event_log (event_timestamp);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_user_id ON pos.application_event_log (user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_event_log_session_id ON pos.application_event_log (session_id);

-- Log function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_log_application_event(
    p_application_id UUID,
    p_event_type VARCHAR(50),
    p_event_data JSONB DEFAULT NULL,
    p_ip_address INET DEFAULT NULL,
    p_user_agent TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    p_session_id VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS UUID
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_event_log_id UUID;
    v_user_id UUID;
BEGIN
    -- Get current user
    v_user_id := current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID;

    -- Insert event log entry
    INSERT INTO pos.application_event_log (
        application_id,
        user_id,
        event_type,
        event_data,
        event_timestamp,
        ip_address,
        user_agent,
        session_id,
        created_at
    ) VALUES (
        p_application_id,
        v_user_id,
        p_event_type,
        p_event_data,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        COALESCE(p_ip_address, inet_client_addr()),
        COALESCE(p_user_agent, current_setting('app.user_agent', TRUE)),
        COALESCE(p_session_id, current_setting('app.session_id', TRUE)),
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    ) RETURNING application_event_log_id INTO v_event_log_id;

    RETURN v_event_log_id;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error logging application event: %', SQLERRM;
        RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_log_application_event IS 'Logs application events for audit and analytics';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB112 - fn_get_application_summary
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB112 - fn_get_application_summary
-- Description: Returns a comprehensive summary of an application for dashboard display
-- Business Case: This function aggregates data from multiple tables to provide a single, comprehensive view of an application's status, borrower information, financial details, and milestones. It eliminates the need for multiple separate queries, reducing application complexity and improving performance. The summary includes application status, borrower names, loan amount, DTI, LTV, AUS status, disclosure status, and task completion. This consolidated view is essential for the LO pipeline dashboard and borrower portal.
-- KPIs: Dashboard load time, Query complexity reduction, Data consistency, Application summary accuracy, Dashboard user satisfaction
-- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_get_application_summary(
    p_application_id UUID
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_summary JSONB;
    v_borrower_names TEXT[];
    v_task_count INTEGER;
    v_completed_tasks INTEGER;
    v_aus_status TEXT;
    v_dti_record RECORD;
    v_document_count INTEGER;
    v_workflow_step TEXT;
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_application_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Application ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get borrower names
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name)
    INTO v_borrower_names
    FROM pos.application_borrower ab
    JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
    WHERE ab.application_id = p_application_id
      AND ab.role_type IN ('PRIMARY_BORROWER', 'CO_BORROWER');

    -- Get task counts
    SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed THEN 1 END)
    INTO v_task_count, v_completed_tasks
    FROM pos.task
    WHERE application_id = p_application_id
      AND status != 'CANCELLED';

    -- Get AUS status
    SELECT a.finding_type::TEXT INTO v_aus_status
    FROM pos.aus_submission a
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id
      AND a.is_active = TRUE
    ORDER BY a.submission_timestamp DESC
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Get DTI
    SELECT * INTO v_dti_record
    FROM pos.fn_calculate_dti(p_application_id)
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Get document count
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_document_count
    FROM pos.document_upload
    WHERE application_id = p_application_id
      AND is_active = TRUE;

    -- Get current workflow step
    SELECT current_step INTO v_workflow_step
    FROM pos.application_workflow_state
    WHERE application_id = p_application_id
      AND is_completed = FALSE
    ORDER BY created_at DESC
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Build summary JSON
    v_summary := jsonb_build_object(
        'application_id', p_application_id,
        'loan_number', (SELECT loan_number FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'status', (SELECT status::TEXT FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'borrower_names', v_borrower_names,
        'loan_amount', (SELECT loan_amount FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'interest_rate', (SELECT interest_rate FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'dti_front', v_dti_record.front_end_ratio,
        'dti_back', v_dti_record.back_end_ratio,
        'dti_status', v_dti_record.dti_status,
        'ltv', (SELECT ltv_ratio FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'aus_status', v_aus_status,
        'workflow_step', v_workflow_step,
        'task_count', v_task_count,
        'completed_tasks', v_completed_tasks,
        'task_completion_percent', CASE
            WHEN v_task_count > 0 THEN ROUND((v_completed_tasks * 100.0 / v_task_count), 2)
            ELSE 100
        END,
        'document_count', v_document_count,
        'submitted_date', (SELECT submitted_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'created_date', (SELECT created_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id),
        'days_since_created', EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (SELECT created_date FROM pos.application WHERE application_id = p_application_id))),
        'rate_lock_status', (SELECT lock_status FROM pos.rate_lock_history WHERE application_id = p_application_id ORDER BY lock_date DESC LIMIT 1)
    );

    RETURN v_summary;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error getting application summary for %: %', p_application_id, SQLERRM;
        RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', SQLERRM, 'application_id', p_application_id);
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_get_application_summary IS 'Returns a comprehensive summary of an application for dashboard display';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB113 - fn_calculate_dti
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB113 - fn_calculate_dti
-- Description: Database function to compute front-end and back-end Debt-to-Income ratios
-- Business Case: The fn_calculate_dti function is a centralized, immutable database function that encapsulates the exact mathematical logic and GSE rules for calculating a borrower's Debt-to-Income ratio. It accepts an application ID as input, retrieves the relevant income, liability, and housing expense data, applies the correct qualifying formulas, and returns the front-end and back-end DTI ratios. This function is the single source of truth for DTI logic, ensuring that the real-time POS calculator, the AUS submission engine, and the underwriting QC module all use the exact same math. It handles complex scenarios like variable income annualization, non-occupant co-borrower liability splitting, and rental income offsets. By encapsulating this logic in the database, it eliminates the risk of divergent calculations occurring in different microservices, ensuring mathematical consistency across the entire unified data fabric.
-- KPIs: DTI calculation consistency rate, Regulatory update deployment time, Calculation execution latency, Underwriter DTI override rate, Borrower DTI shock reduction
-- Feature Reference: F-60
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_calculate_dti(
    p_application_id UUID,
    p_include_rental_income BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    p_calculation_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    front_end_ratio NUMERIC(5,2),
    back_end_ratio NUMERIC(5,2),
    gross_monthly_income NUMERIC(18,2),
    total_housing_expense NUMERIC(12,2),
    total_monthly_debt NUMERIC(18,2),
    dti_status VARCHAR(20),
    calculation_id UUID
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_gross_income NUMERIC(18,2) := 0;
    v_housing_expense NUMERIC(12,2) := 0;
    v_total_debt NUMERIC(18,2) := 0;
    v_rental_income NUMERIC(12,2) := 0;
    v_borrower_record RECORD;
    v_calculation_id UUID;
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_application_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Application ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get total income from all borrowers on the application
    FOR v_borrower_record IN (
        SELECT DISTINCT ab.borrower_id
        FROM pos.application_borrower ab
        WHERE ab.application_id = p_application_id
    ) LOOP
        -- Get primary income
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(e.base_income), 0)
        INTO v_gross_income
        FROM pos.employment e
        WHERE e.borrower_id = v_borrower_record.borrower_id
          AND e.is_current = TRUE
          AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date > CURRENT_DATE);

        -- Add income projection for variable income if available
        SELECT COALESCE(ip.projected_annual_income / 12, 0)
        INTO v_gross_income
        FROM pos.income_projection ip
        WHERE ip.employment_id IN (
            SELECT employment_id FROM pos.employment WHERE borrower_id = v_borrower_record.borrower_id AND is_current = TRUE
        )
        ORDER BY ip.calculation_date DESC
        LIMIT 1;

        -- Get rental income if applicable
        IF p_include_rental_income THEN
            SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ri.net_monthly_rental_income), 0)
            INTO v_rental_income
            FROM pos.rental_income ri
            JOIN pos.property p ON p.property_id = ri.property_id
            WHERE p.application_id = p_application_id
              AND ri.verification_status = 'COMPLETED';

            v_gross_income := v_gross_income + v_rental_income;
        END IF;

        -- Get total debt (liabilities)
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(l.monthly_payment), 0)
        INTO v_total_debt
        FROM pos.liability l
        WHERE l.borrower_id = v_borrower_record.borrower_id
          AND l.is_active = TRUE;

        -- Add dependent care expenses to debt
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(dce.monthly_amount), 0)
        INTO v_total_debt
        FROM pos.dependent_care_expense dce
        JOIN pos.dependent d ON d.dependent_id = dce.dependent_id
        WHERE d.borrower_id = v_borrower_record.borrower_id
          AND dce.is_active = TRUE;
    END LOOP;

    -- Get housing expense (PITI) from escrow_piti_component
    SELECT COALESCE(ep.total_monthly_payment, 0)
    INTO v_housing_expense
    FROM pos.escrow_piti_component ep
    WHERE ep.application_id = p_application_id
      AND ep.is_current = TRUE
    ORDER BY ep.created_at DESC
    LIMIT 1;

    -- Generate calculation ID
    v_calculation_id := uuid_generate_v4();

    -- Return results
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        ROUND(CAST(v_housing_expense AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(v_gross_income, 0) * 100, 2) AS front_end_ratio,
        ROUND(CAST(v_housing_expense + v_total_debt AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(v_gross_income, 0) * 100, 2) AS back_end_ratio,
        v_gross_income AS gross_monthly_income,
        v_housing_expense AS total_housing_expense,
        v_total_debt AS total_monthly_debt,
        CASE
            WHEN v_gross_income = 0 THEN 'NO_INCOME'
            WHEN ROUND(CAST(v_housing_expense + v_total_debt AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(v_gross_income, 0) * 100, 2) > 43 THEN 'EXCEEDS_QM_LIMIT'
            WHEN ROUND(CAST(v_housing_expense + v_total_debt AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(v_gross_income, 0) * 100, 2) > 36 THEN 'EXCEEDS_CONVENTIONAL_LIMIT'
            ELSE 'WITHIN_LIMITS'
        END AS dti_status,
        v_calculation_id AS calculation_id;

    -- Handle no income case
    IF v_gross_income = 0 THEN
        RETURN QUERY
        SELECT
            0.00 AS front_end_ratio,
            0.00 AS back_end_ratio,
            0.00 AS gross_monthly_income,
            0.00 AS total_housing_expense,
            0.00 AS total_monthly_debt,
            'NO_INCOME' AS dti_status,
            v_calculation_id AS calculation_id;
    END IF;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error calculating DTI for application %: %', p_application_id, SQLERRM;
        RETURN QUERY
        SELECT
            NULL::NUMERIC(5,2),
            NULL::NUMERIC(5,2),
            NULL::NUMERIC(18,2),
            NULL::NUMERIC(12,2),
            NULL::NUMERIC(18,2),
            'ERROR'::VARCHAR(20),
            NULL::UUID;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_calculate_dti IS 'Database function to compute front-end and back-end Debt-to-Income ratios with GSE rule compliance';

-- ====================================================================================
-- VIEW: DB114 - vw_application_pipeline
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- View: DB114 - vw_application_pipeline
-- Description: Comprehensive view of the application pipeline for dashboard reporting
-- Business Case: The application_pipeline view provides a comprehensive, real-time view of all applications in the pipeline, including application details, borrower information, status, AUS results, and key metrics. This view is the foundation for the LO dashboard, pipeline management, and executive reporting. It aggregates data from multiple tables into a single, easy-to-query view, eliminating complex joins and improving dashboard performance. By providing a single source of truth for pipeline data, it ensures consistency across all reporting and analytics.
-- KPIs: Pipeline visibility, Dashboard load time, Data consistency, Operational decision speed, Forecast accuracy
-- Feature Reference: F-06, F-22, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_application_pipeline AS
SELECT
    a.application_id,
    a.loan_number,
    a.loan_purpose,
    a.loan_amount,
    a.interest_rate,
    a.status,
    a.created_date,
    a.submitted_date,
    a.clear_to_close_date,
    a.closed_date,
    a.created_by AS lo_user_id,
    a.referral_source,
    a.lead_source,

    -- Borrower information
    (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name)
     FROM pos.application_borrower ab
     JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
     WHERE ab.application_id = a.application_id
       AND ab.role_type IN ('PRIMARY_BORROWER', 'CO_BORROWER')) AS borrower_names,

    -- Key metrics
    dti.front_end_ratio,
    dti.back_end_ratio,
    dti.dti_status,
    a.ltv_ratio,

    -- AUS status
    (SELECT finding_type::TEXT
     FROM pos.aus_submission aus
     WHERE aus.application_id = a.application_id
       AND aus.is_active = TRUE
     ORDER BY aus.submission_timestamp DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS aus_status,

    -- Task completion
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND status != 'CANCELLED') AS total_tasks,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.task WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND is_completed = TRUE) AS completed_tasks,

    -- Document status
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.document_upload WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND is_active = TRUE) AS total_documents,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.document_upload WHERE application_id = a.application_id AND ocr_status = 'CLASSIFIED') AS classified_documents,

    -- Rate lock status
    (SELECT lock_status FROM pos.rate_lock_history WHERE application_id = a.application_id ORDER BY lock_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS rate_lock_status,

    -- Days in pipeline
    EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date))::INTEGER AS days_in_pipeline,

    -- Age category
    CASE
        WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 7 THEN '0-7 Days'
        WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 15 THEN '8-15 Days'
        WHEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - a.created_date)) <= 30 THEN '16-30 Days'
        ELSE '30+ Days'
    END AS age_category,

    -- Fraud risk
    (SELECT fraud_risk_category FROM pos.fraud_detection_log WHERE application_id = a.application_id ORDER BY detection_timestamp DESC LIMIT 1) AS fraud_risk,

    -- Created date parts for grouping
    DATE_TRUNC('day', a.created_date) AS created_day,
    DATE_TRUNC('week', a.created_date) AS created_week,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', a.created_date) AS created_month,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM a.created_date) AS created_year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM a.created_date) AS created_month_num

FROM pos.application a
LEFT JOIN pos.fn_calculate_dti(a.application_id) dti ON TRUE
WHERE a.status NOT IN ('DRAFT')
  AND a.status NOT IN ('CLOSED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED')
ORDER BY a.created_date DESC;

COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_application_pipeline IS 'Comprehensive view of the application pipeline for dashboard reporting and pipeline management';

-- ====================================================================================
-- VIEW: DB115 - vw_borrower_portal_dashboard
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- View: DB115 - vw_borrower_portal_dashboard
-- Description: View for borrower portal dashboard showing application status and tasks
-- Business Case: The borrower_portal_dashboard view provides a comprehensive, borrower-friendly view of their application status, tasks, and milestones. It aggregates data from multiple tables into a single view optimized for the borrower portal experience. The view includes the application status, upcoming tasks, recent activity, and key milestones. By providing a single source of truth for the borrower portal, it ensures consistency and reduces the complexity of building the portal interface.
-- KPIs: Portal load time, Borrower engagement rate, Task completion rate, Portal satisfaction score, Portal feature adoption
-- Feature Reference: F-51, F-52, F-65, F-118
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_borrower_portal_dashboard AS
SELECT
    a.application_id,
    a.loan_number,
    a.status,
    a.loan_amount,
    a.interest_rate,
    a.ltv_ratio,
    a.created_date,
    a.submitted_date,
    a.clear_to_close_date,

    -- Borrower info
    b.borrower_id,
    b.first_name,
    b.last_name,
    b.email,
    b.phone,

    -- Tasks
    t.task_count AS total_tasks,
    t.completed_count AS completed_tasks,
    t.overdue_count AS overdue_tasks,
    CASE
        WHEN t.task_count > 0 THEN ROUND((t.completed_count * 100.0 / t.task_count), 2)
        ELSE 100
    END AS task_completion_percent,

    -- Documents
    d.total_documents,
    d.uploaded_documents,

    -- Recent activity
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(row_to_json(activity))
     FROM (
         SELECT action_type, event_timestamp
         FROM pos.borrower_activity_log
         WHERE borrower_id = b.borrower_id
         ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
         LIMIT 5
     ) activity) AS recent_activity,

    -- Next steps
    (SELECT row_to_json(next_step)
     FROM (
         SELECT task_name, due_date, task_priority
         FROM pos.task
         WHERE application_id = a.application_id
           AND is_completed = FALSE
           AND status != 'CANCELLED'
         ORDER BY task_priority ASC, due_date ASC
         LIMIT 1
     ) next_step) AS next_step,

    -- AUS status
    (SELECT finding_type::TEXT || ' - ' || finding_description
     FROM pos.aus_submission
     WHERE application_id = a.application_id
       AND is_active = TRUE
     ORDER BY submission_timestamp DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS aus_status,

    -- Rate lock status
    (SELECT lock_status FROM pos.rate_lock_history
     WHERE application_id = a.application_id
     ORDER BY lock_date DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS rate_lock_status,

    -- Notifications
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos.notification_log
     WHERE borrower_id = b.borrower_id
       AND delivery_status = 'SENT'
       AND opened_at IS NULL) AS unread_notifications,

    -- Workflow progress
    (SELECT current_step FROM pos.application_workflow_state
     WHERE application_id = a.application_id
       AND is_completed = FALSE
     ORDER BY created_at DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS current_workflow_step

FROM pos.application a
JOIN pos.application_borrower ab ON ab.application_id = a.application_id
JOIN pos.borrower b ON b.borrower_id = ab.borrower_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        application_id,
        COUNT(*) AS task_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed THEN 1 END) AS completed_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN is_completed = FALSE AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE THEN 1 END) AS overdue_count
    FROM pos.task
    WHERE status != 'CANCELLED'
    GROUP BY application_id
) t ON t.application_id = a.application_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        application_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_documents,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN ocr_status != 'UPLOADED' THEN 1 END) AS uploaded_documents
    FROM pos.document_upload
    WHERE is_active = TRUE
    GROUP BY application_id
) d ON d.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE ab.role_type IN ('PRIMARY_BORROWER', 'CO_BORROWER');

COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_borrower_portal_dashboard IS 'View for borrower portal dashboard showing application status and tasks';

-- ====================================================================================
-- VIEW: DB116 - vw_application_metrics
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- View: DB116 - vw_application_metrics
-- Description: Aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards
-- Business Case: The application_metrics view provides aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards, including application volume, conversion rates, cycle times, and quality metrics. It aggregates data across all applications, providing executives with a high-level view of pipeline health and performance. This view is the foundation for executive dashboards and strategic reporting.
-- KPIs: Dashboard load time, Metric accuracy, Decision-making speed, Strategic alignment, Executive satisfaction
-- Feature Reference: F-22, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pos.vw_application_metrics AS
WITH app_stats AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('day', created_date) AS day,
        DATE_TRUNC('week', created_date) AS week,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', created_date) AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS total_applications,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'SUBMITTED' THEN 1 END) AS submitted_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('AUS_APPROVED', 'CONDITIONAL_APPROVAL') THEN 1 END) AS approved_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'CLEAR_TO_CLOSE' THEN 1 END) AS clear_to_close_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'CLOSED' THEN 1 END) AS closed_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('WITHDRAWN', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED') THEN 1 END) AS fallout_count,
        AVG(EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CASE
            WHEN closed_date IS NOT NULL THEN closed_date - submitted_date
            ELSE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - submitted_date
        END))) AS avg_cycle_days,
        AVG(a.loan_amount) AS avg_loan_amount,
        SUM(a.loan_amount) AS total_loan_volume,
        AVG(a.ltv_ratio) AS avg_ltv,
        AVG(dti.back_end_ratio) AS avg_dti
    FROM pos.application a
    LEFT JOIN pos.fn_calculate_dti(a.application_id) dti ON TRUE
    WHERE created_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
    GROUP BY ROLLUP (DATE_TRUNC('day', created_date), DATE_TRUNC('week', created_date), DATE_TRUNC('month', created_date))
)
SELECT
    day,
    week,
    month,
    total_applications,
    submitted_count,
    approved_count,
    clear_to_close_count,
    closed_count,
    fallout_count,
    ROUND(CAST(closed_count AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(submitted_count, 0) * 100, 2) AS conversion_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(fallout_count AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(submitted_count, 0) * 100, 2) AS fallout_rate,
    ROUND(avg_cycle_days, 1) AS avg_cycle_days,
    ROUND(avg_loan_amount, 2) AS avg_loan_amount,
    ROUND(total_loan_volume, 2) AS total_loan_volume,
    ROUND(avg_ltv, 2) AS avg_ltv,
    ROUND(avg_dti, 2) AS avg_dti
FROM app_stats
ORDER BY day DESC NULLS LAST;

COMMENT ON VIEW pos.vw_application_metrics IS 'Aggregated application metrics for executive dashboards';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB117 - fn_cleanup_expired_data
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB117 - fn_cleanup_expired_data
-- Description: Cleanup function for expired data and orphaned records
-- Business Case: The fn_cleanup_expired_data function is a maintenance function that cleans up expired data and orphaned records to maintain database health and performance. It handles tasks such as archiving old application data, deleting expired sessions, cleaning up orphaned audit logs, and managing data retention. This function should be scheduled to run periodically as part of database maintenance.
-- KPIs: Data cleanup effectiveness, Database performance improvement, Storage cost reduction, Cleanup automation rate, Maintenance overhead reduction
-- Feature Reference: F-44, F-112
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_cleanup_expired_data(
    p_dry_run BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    p_older_than_days INTEGER DEFAULT 90
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    cleanup_action VARCHAR(50),
    records_affected INTEGER,
    cleanup_message TEXT,
    execution_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_records_affected INTEGER;
    v_action VARCHAR(50);
    v_message TEXT;
    v_start_time TIMESTAMP := clock_timestamp();
BEGIN
    -- Clean up expired sessions
    v_action := 'EXPIRED_SESSIONS';
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        DELETE FROM pos.visitor_session
        WHERE session_end < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL
          AND session_abandoned = TRUE;
        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
    ELSE
        SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
        FROM pos.visitor_session
        WHERE session_end < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL
          AND session_abandoned = TRUE;
    END IF;
    v_message := 'Cleaned up expired sessions older than ' || p_older_than_days || ' days';
    cleanup_action := v_action;
    records_affected := v_records_affected;
    cleanup_message := v_message;
    execution_time := clock_timestamp();
    RETURN NEXT;

    -- Clean up expired magic links
    v_action := 'EXPIRED_MAGIC_LINKS';
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        DELETE FROM pos.magic_link_log
        WHERE expiry_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND is_used = FALSE
          AND is_revoked = FALSE;
        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
    ELSE
        SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
        FROM pos.magic_link_log
        WHERE expiry_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND is_used = FALSE
          AND is_revoked = FALSE;
    END IF;
    v_message := 'Cleaned up expired magic links';
    cleanup_action := v_action;
    records_affected := v_records_affected;
    cleanup_message := v_message;
    execution_time := clock_timestamp();
    RETURN NEXT;

    -- Clean up expired secure links
    v_action := 'EXPIRED_SECURE_LINKS';
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        UPDATE pos.secure_link_expiry
        SET is_active = FALSE,
            is_revoked = TRUE,
            revocation_reason = 'Auto-expired by cleanup job'
        WHERE expires_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND is_active = TRUE;
        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
    ELSE
        SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
        FROM pos.secure_link_expiry
        WHERE expires_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND is_active = TRUE;
    END IF;
    v_message := 'Expired secure links deactivated';
    cleanup_action := v_action;
    records_affected := v_records_affected;
    cleanup_message := v_message;
    execution_time := clock_timestamp();
    RETURN NEXT;

    -- Clean up orphaned activity logs
    v_action := 'ORPHANED_ACTIVITY_LOGS';
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        DELETE FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.visitor_session vs
            WHERE vs.visitor_session_id = bal.visitor_session_id
        )
        AND bal.event_timestamp < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL;
        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
    ELSE
        SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
        FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.visitor_session vs
            WHERE vs.visitor_session_id = bal.visitor_session_id
        )
        AND bal.event_timestamp < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - (p_older_than_days || ' days')::INTERVAL;
    END IF;
    v_message := 'Cleaned up orphaned activity logs';
    cleanup_action := v_action;
    records_affected := v_records_affected;
    cleanup_message := v_message;
    execution_time := clock_timestamp();
    RETURN NEXT;

    -- Clean up expired rate locks
    v_action := 'EXPIRED_RATE_LOCKS';
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        UPDATE pos.rate_lock_history
        SET lock_status = 'EXPIRED',
            updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        WHERE lock_expiration_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND lock_status = 'ACTIVE';
        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_records_affected = ROW_COUNT;
    ELSE
        SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_records_affected
        FROM pos.rate_lock_history
        WHERE lock_expiration_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
          AND lock_status = 'ACTIVE';
    END IF;
    v_message := 'Expired rate locks deactivated';
    cleanup_action := v_action;
    records_affected := v_records_affected;
    cleanup_message := v_message;
    execution_time := clock_timestamp();
    RETURN NEXT;

    -- Log the cleanup operation
    IF NOT p_dry_run THEN
        PERFORM pos.fn_log_application_event(
            NULL,
            'SYSTEM_CLEANUP',
            jsonb_build_object(
                'action', 'CLEANUP_EXPIRED_DATA',
                'older_than_days', p_older_than_days,
                'timestamp', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                'duration_ms', EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM (clock_timestamp() - v_start_time))
            )
        );
    END IF;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error in cleanup job: %', SQLERRM;
        cleanup_action := 'ERROR';
        records_affected := 0;
        cleanup_message := SQLERRM;
        execution_time := clock_timestamp();
        RETURN NEXT;
        RETURN;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_cleanup_expired_data IS 'Cleanup function for expired data and orphaned records';

-- ====================================================================================
-- FUNCTION: DB118 - fn_borrower_activity_summary
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Function: DB118 - fn_borrower_activity_summary
-- Description: Generates a summary of borrower activity for analytics
-- Business Case: The fn_borrower_activity_summary function generates a comprehensive summary of borrower activity, including session counts, page views, time spent, and interaction patterns. This function is used for user behavior analytics and UX optimization. It provides the data needed to understand borrower behavior and identify opportunities for UX improvement.
-- KPIs: Activity summary generation time, Analytics accuracy, UX improvement velocity, User behavior understanding, Conversion rate improvement
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-72, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.fn_borrower_activity_summary(
    p_borrower_id UUID,
    p_date_from DATE DEFAULT NULL,
    p_date_to DATE DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    metric_name VARCHAR(50),
    metric_value NUMERIC,
    metric_description TEXT,
    metric_timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_total_sessions INTEGER;
    v_total_actions INTEGER;
    v_avg_session_duration NUMERIC;
    v_completion_rate NUMERIC;
    v_abandonment_rate NUMERIC;
    v_time_per_step NUMERIC;
    v_avg_form_time NUMERIC;
    v_device_distribution JSONB;
BEGIN
    -- Validate input
    IF p_borrower_id IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Borrower ID cannot be null';
    END IF;

    -- Get session metrics
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT vs.visitor_session_id),
        COUNT(bal.borrower_activity_log_id),
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(vs.session_end, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - vs.session_start)) / 60)
    INTO v_total_sessions, v_total_actions, v_avg_session_duration
    FROM pos.visitor_session vs
    LEFT JOIN pos.borrower_activity_log bal ON bal.visitor_session_id = vs.visitor_session_id
    WHERE vs.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
      AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR vs.session_start >= p_date_from)
      AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR vs.session_start <= p_date_to);

    -- Get completion rate
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN vs.session_abandoned = FALSE THEN vs.visitor_session_id END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT vs.visitor_session_id), 0)
    INTO v_completion_rate
    FROM pos.visitor_session vs
    WHERE vs.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
      AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR vs.session_start >= p_date_from)
      AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR vs.session_start <= p_date_to);

    -- Get abandonment rate
    v_abandonment_rate := 100 - COALESCE(v_completion_rate, 0);

    -- Get average time per application step
    SELECT
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_timestamp - current_timestamp))) / 60
    INTO v_time_per_step
    FROM (
        SELECT
            bal.event_timestamp AS current_timestamp,
            LEAD(bal.event_timestamp) OVER (ORDER BY bal.event_timestamp) AS next_timestamp
        FROM pos.borrower_activity_log bal
        WHERE bal.borrower_id = p_borrower_id
          AND bal.action_type = 'LOAD'
          AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR bal.event_timestamp >= p_date_from)
          AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR bal.event_timestamp <= p_date_to)
    ) step_times
    WHERE next_timestamp IS NOT NULL;

    -- Get average form completion time
    SELECT
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (completion_time - start_time)) / 60)
    INTO v_avg_form_time
    FROM (
        SELECT
            MIN(CASE WHEN action_type = 'FOCUS' THEN event_timestamp END) AS start_time,
            MAX(CASE WHEN action_type = 'SUBMIT' THEN event_timestamp END) AS completion_time
        FROM pos.borrower_activity_log
        WHERE borrower_id = p_borrower_id
          AND action_type IN ('FOCUS', 'SUBMIT')
          AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR event_timestamp >= p_date_from)
          AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR event_timestamp <= p_date_to)
        GROUP BY visitor_session_id
    ) form_times
    WHERE completion_time IS NOT NULL AND start_time IS NOT NULL;

    -- Get device distribution
    SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT device_type)
    INTO v_device_distribution
    FROM pos.visitor_session
    WHERE borrower_id = p_borrower_id
      AND (p_date_from IS NULL OR session_start >= p_date_from)
      AND (p_date_to IS NULL OR session_start <= p_date_to);

    -- Return results
    metric_name := 'total_sessions';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_total_sessions, 0);
    metric_description := 'Total number of sessions';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'total_actions';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_total_actions, 0);
    metric_description := 'Total number of user actions';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'avg_session_duration_minutes';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_avg_session_duration, 0);
    metric_description := 'Average session duration in minutes';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'session_completion_rate';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_completion_rate, 0);
    metric_description := 'Percentage of sessions that were completed';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'session_abandonment_rate';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_abandonment_rate, 0);
    metric_description := 'Percentage of sessions that were abandoned';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'avg_time_per_step_minutes';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_time_per_step, 0);
    metric_description := 'Average time spent per application step in minutes';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'avg_form_completion_time_minutes';
    metric_value := COALESCE(v_avg_form_time, 0);
    metric_description := 'Average time to complete forms in minutes';
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

    metric_name := 'device_distribution';
    metric_value := COALESCE((v_device_distribution->>0)::NUMERIC, 0);
    metric_description := 'Device distribution: ' || COALESCE(v_device_distribution::TEXT, 'none');
    metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEXT;

EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE WARNING 'Error generating activity summary for borrower %: %', p_borrower_id, SQLERRM;
        metric_name := 'error';
        metric_value := 0;
        metric_description := SQLERRM;
        metric_timestamp := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
        RETURN NEXT;
        RETURN;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.fn_borrower_activity_summary IS 'Generates a summary of borrower activity for analytics';

-- ====================================================================================
-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY POLICIES
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RLS Policies for POS tables
-- Description: Row Level Security policies to enforce data isolation and access control
-- Business Case: RLS policies ensure that users can only access data they are authorized to see. This is critical for a multi-tenant platform where different lenders and users need to be isolated from each other's data. The policies enforce the principle of least privilege, ensuring that Loan Officers can only see their own applications, borrowers can only see their own data, and administrators have appropriate access. This security architecture is essential for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 compliance and builds trust with enterprise customers.
-- Feature Reference: F-09, F-71, F-84
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Enable RLS on core tables
ALTER TABLE pos.application ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.borrower ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.application_borrower ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.document_upload ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.econsent_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.field_change_history ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.notification_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.rate_lock_history ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE pos.fraud_detection_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Create policy for application table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS application_isolation_policy ON pos.application;
CREATE POLICY application_isolation_policy ON pos.application
    USING (
        -- System admin can see everything
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        -- Loan Officer can see their own applications
        created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        -- Borrower can see applications they are associated with
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_borrower ab
            WHERE ab.application_id = application.application_id
            AND ab.borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
        OR
        -- Processor/Underwriter can see applications assigned to them
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_workflow_state aws
            WHERE aws.application_id = application.application_id
            AND aws.current_step_status IN ('IN_PROGRESS', 'PENDING')
            AND aws.step_data->>'assigned_to' = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::TEXT
        )
    );

-- Create policy for borrower table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS borrower_isolation_policy ON pos.borrower;
CREATE POLICY borrower_isolation_policy ON pos.borrower
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_borrower ab
            WHERE ab.borrower_id = borrower.borrower_id
            AND EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
                WHERE a.application_id = ab.application_id
                AND (a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
                     OR EXISTS (
                         SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_workflow_state aws
                         WHERE aws.application_id = a.application_id
                         AND aws.step_data->>'assigned_to' = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::TEXT
                     ))
            )
        )
    );

-- Create policy for notification_log table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS notification_log_isolation_policy ON pos.notification_log;
CREATE POLICY notification_log_isolation_policy ON pos.notification_log
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        borrower_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = notification_log.application_id
            AND (a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
                 OR EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_workflow_state aws
                     WHERE aws.application_id = a.application_id
                     AND aws.step_data->>'assigned_to' = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::TEXT
                 ))
        )
    );

-- Create policy for rate_lock_history table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS rate_lock_history_isolation_policy ON pos.rate_lock_history;
CREATE POLICY rate_lock_history_isolation_policy ON pos.rate_lock_history
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = rate_lock_history.application_id
            AND (a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
                 OR EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM pos.application_workflow_state aws
                     WHERE aws.application_id = a.application_id
                     AND aws.step_data->>'assigned_to' = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::TEXT
                 ))
        )
    );

-- Create policy for fraud_detection_log table
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS fraud_detection_log_isolation_policy ON pos.fraud_detection_log;
CREATE POLICY fraud_detection_log_isolation_policy ON pos.fraud_detection_log
    USING (
        current_setting('app.is_super_user', TRUE)::BOOLEAN = TRUE
        OR
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM pos.application a
            WHERE a.application_id = fraud_detection_log.application_id
            AND a.created_by = current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID
        )
        OR
        current_setting('app.current_user_role', TRUE) = 'UNDERWRITER'
        OR
        current_setting('app.current_user_role', TRUE) = 'COMPLIANCE_OFFICER'
    );

-- ====================================================================================
-- TRIGGER: trg_update_updated_at
-- ====================================================================================
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Trigger: trg_update_updated_at
-- Description: Generic trigger to automatically update updated_at timestamp on any row change
-- Business Case: The trg_update_updated_at is a generic trigger that automatically updates the updated_at timestamp column on any row in a table that has such a column. This trigger ensures that the last modification time is always accurate, providing a reliable audit trail for data changes. It eliminates the need for application code to manually set the updated_at field, reducing the risk of human error and ensuring consistency across all tables. This trigger is applied to all core tables that have created_at and updated_at columns.
-- Feature Reference: F-13, F-98, F-117
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at := CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEW;
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at IS 'Generic trigger to automatically update updated_at timestamp on any row change';

-- Apply trigger to all core tables with updated_at column
DO $$
DECLARE
    v_table_name TEXT;
BEGIN
    FOR v_table_name IN (
        SELECT table_name
        FROM information_schema.tables
        WHERE table_schema = 'pos'
          AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE'
    ) LOOP
        IF EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM information_schema.columns
            WHERE table_schema = 'pos'
              AND table_name = v_table_name
              AND column_name = 'updated_at'
        ) THEN
            EXECUTE format('
                DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_update_updated_at_%I ON pos.%I;
                CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_updated_at_%I
                    BEFORE UPDATE ON pos.%I
                    FOR EACH ROW
                    EXECUTE FUNCTION pos.trg_update_updated_at();
            ', v_table_name, v_table_name, v_table_name, v_table_name);
        END IF;
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;
